SECT 35.55 Commissioner's discretion ### INCOME TAX ASSESSMENT ACT 1997 - SECT 35.55 **Commissioner's discretion** (1) The Commissioner may, on application, decide that the rule in [subsection](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s40.122.html#subsection)35 \- 10(2) does not apply to a \\* [business](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.15.html#business) activity for one or more [income years](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_year) (the excluded years ) if the Commissioner is satisfied that it would be unreasonable to apply that rule because: (a) the [business](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.15.html#business) activity was or [will](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.5.html#will) be affected in the excluded years by [special](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.15.html#special) circumstances outside the control of the operators of the [business](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.15.html#business) activity, including drought, flood, bushfire or some other natural disaster; or Note: This [paragraph](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s40.185.html#paragraph) is intended to [provide](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#provide) for a case where a [business](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.15.html#business) activity would have satisfied one of the tests if it were not for the [special](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.15.html#special) circumstances. (b) for an applicant who carries on the [business](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.15.html#business) activity who satisfies [subsection](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s40.122.html#subsection)35 \- 10(2E) (income requirement) for the most recent [income year](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_year) ending before the application is made--the [business](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.15.html#business) activity has started to be carried on and, for the excluded years: (i) because of its nature, it has not satisfied, or [will](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.5.html#will) not satisfy, one of the tests set out in section [35](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s35.html)\- 30, [35](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s35.html)\- [35](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s35.html), [35](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s35.html)\- 40 or [35](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s35.html)\- [45](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s45.html); and (ii) there is an objective expectation, based on evidence from independent sources (where available) that, within a period that is commercially viable for the industry concerned, the activity [will](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.5.html#will) either meet one of those tests or [will](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.5.html#will) produce assessable income for an [income year](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_year) [greater](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#greater) than the [deductions](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.15.html#deduction) attributable to it for that year (apart from the operation of [subsections](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s40.122.html#subsection)35 \- 10(2) and (2C)); and (ii) there is an objective expectation, based on evidence from independent sources (where available) that, within a period that is commercially viable for the industry concerned, the activity [will](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.5.html#will) produce assessable income for an [income year](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_year) [greater](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#greater) than the [deductions](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.15.html#deduction) attributable to it for that year (apart from the operation of [subsections](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s40.122.html#subsection)35 \- 10(2) and (2C)). correctness.justification: Conclusions on items 2 and 3 and the Division 35 outcome match the reference: $800 denied under s 32-5 with item 4.3 failing the 'greater opportunity' exclusion; $1,500 deductible under s 32-35 item 2.1 (4-hour seminar); loss of $15,000 deferred under s 35-10 with the $250,000 income requirement met and all four tests plus the s 35-55 discretion correctly analysed and failed. Item 1 diverges from the reference's unqualified 'deductible' by adding an overnight-stay condition — a defensible, practice-accurate refinement (and the 'not entertainment' analysis matches the reference) — but it is a qualification the reference does not impose and rests on an uncaptured ATO page and an uncaptured case (Cooper). Statutory rules are stated from the legislation itself with operative words quoted.

completeness.justification: Every reference point is covered and extended: the Div 32 framework, item 4.3's public-promotion failure for the $800, the s 32-35/s 32-65 seminar analysis (including breaks not counted, the business-meeting exclusion and the promotional-purpose exclusion (b) that the reference glosses over), the loss computation, annualisation to $10,000 under s 35-30(b), all four tests in a workings table, both limbs of the s 35-55 discretion (which the reference omits), the deferral/carry-forward mechanics, Joe's resulting $60,000 taxable income, and the adjustment if the $800 sits inside the accountant's $20,000. No judicial authority decides any point in the reference, so none was required; the two cases mentioned are extras.

faithfulness.justification: Roughly 85-90% of load-bearing claims are anchored at the claim and verified from captured text: s 32-5 ([[1]]), s 32-10 definition and notes ([[2]]), TR 97/17 paras 21, 23, 108 and the client-lunch table row ([[3]]), item 4.3 and its exclusion ([[5]]), s 32-20 ([[6]]), s 32-35 item 2.1 with exclusions ([[7]]), s 32-65(1)-(3) ([[8]]), s 35-10(1), (2) and (2E) ([[9]]), s 35-30 with the part-year estimate limb ([[10]]), seasonality and the test thresholds ([[11]]), and s 35-55(1)(a)-(b) including the hardwood-trees note ([[12]]). Unverified: the quoted ATO 'meals, if you are away overnight' line ([[4]], page not captured), the Cooper day-trip proposition (no capture, no marker), the Softwood Pulp aside, and the profits/real-property/other-assets thresholds, which are verified only via the secondary ATO page with the [[11]] marker not anchored to those table rows.

helpfulness.justification: Directly answers for the 2022-23 year with a short answer, per-item analysis, quoted statutory words, a workings table for the four tests, and a concrete closing list of facts to confirm with Joe — the working elements of professional advice. Minor polish issues only: the hedged first bullet is less decisive than a partner might like, and first-person asides ('I have not checked…', 'my reading of s 35-10') slightly undercut authority, though the substantive caveats themselves are appropriate.

citation_grounding.justification: Citations are densely anchored at the claim and overwhelmingly verified from captured primary text: the operative words of ss 32-5, 32-10, 32-20, 32-35, 32-45, 32-65, 35-10, 35-30 and 35-55 are all in the captures, as is the whole of TR 97/17 and the ATO four-tests page. Held below 5 by the uncaptured ATO travel page ([[4]]) supporting the overnight-meals claim, the secondary-only grounding of the three non-income test thresholds (ss 35-35/40/45 cited by number but never captured), and the two uncaptured case references; no irrelevant or unsupportive citations.

judge_output.summary: Substantively correct, statute-first analysis that matches the reference on items 2, 3 and Division 35 and adds genuine value (s 35-55 discretion, workings table), with dense claim-anchored citations mostly verified from captured legislation; its only real departure is the hedged overnight-stay condition on the $150 meals, supported only by unverified sources.

(3) However, an amount of expenditure on \\* in \- house software can only be allocated to a software development pool if you intend to use the software solely for a \\* [taxable purpose](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#taxable_purpose). (4) You [must](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.15.html#must) create a separate software development pool for [each](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.15.html#each) [income year](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_year) for [which](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.5.html#which) you incur amounts of the kind referred to in [subsection](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s87.40.html#subsection)(1). #### Navigate -     extract (page read): [Skip to main content](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/income-deductions-and-concessions/depreciation-and-capital-expenses-and-allowances/other-capital-asset-and-expense-deductions/in-house-software#content) [Skip To search](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/income-deductions-and-concessions/depreciation-and-capital-expenses-and-allowances/other-capital-asset-and-expense-deductions/in-house-software#search-box) [Skip To Alex Virtual Assistant](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/income-deductions-and-concessions/depreciation-and-capital-expenses-and-allowances/other-capital-asset-and-expense-deductions/in-house-software#alex-virtual-assistant) # In-house software Expenses for in-house software may be deducted in a number of different ways depending on the circumstances. **Last updated** 27 June 2025 Print or Download ## On this page - [Business costs](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/income-deductions-and-concessions/depreciation-and-capital-expenses-and-allowances/other-capital-asset-and-expense-deductions/in-house-software#ato-Businesscosts) - [Software development pools](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/income-deductions-and-concessions/depreciation-and-capital-expenses-and-allowances/other-capital-asset-and-expense-deductions/in-house-software#ato-Softwaredevelopmentpools) - [Disposal of in-house software](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/income-deductions-and-concessions/depreciation-and-capital-expenses-and-allowances/other-capital-asset-and-expense-deductions/in-house-software#ato-Disposalofinhousesoftware) In-house software is computer software, or the right to use computer software that you acquire, develop or have someone else develop for your business use, not for sale. It does not include commercial off-the-shelf software if the software has an effective life of one year or less, or periodic payments made to use software in your business. These costs are deductible in the year incurred. In-house software is only deductible under the uniform capital allowances (UCA) rules or the simplified depreciation rules for small business entities. Deductions for in-house software may be claimed in a number of ways depending on the circumstances: - [Business costs](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/income-deductions-and-concessions/depreciation-and-capital-expenses-and-allowances/other-capital-asset-and-expense-deductions/in-house-software#businesscosts) - [Software development pools](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/income-deductions-and-concessions/depreciation-and-capital-expenses-and-allowances/other-capital-asset-and-expense-deductions/in-house-software#softwaredevelopmentpools) - [Disposal of in-house software](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/income-deductions-and-concessions/depreciation-and-capital-expenses-and-allowances/other-capital-asset-and-expense-deductions/in-house-software#disposalofinhousesoftware) ## Business costs If you’re a small business you can use the simplified depreciation rules for the purchase and development of software that is installed and ready to use. If the expense was less than the instant asset write-off threshold, you may be able to claim a deduction for the expenditure in the year you incurred it. If the expense is equal to or more than the instant asset write-off threshold, you can depreciate it under the general small business pool rules. If the software is still in development and is not ready for use, you can use the software development pool rules. If you can’t or have chosen not to use the simplified depreciation rules or a software development pool, you can depreciate the value of the software using the prime cost method. The depreciation of the in-house software depends on when you started to hold it: - 5 year effective life if you started to hold it on or after 1 July 2015 - 4 year effective life if you started to hold it between 7:30 pm AEST on 13 May 2008 and 30 June 2015. **Next steps** - [Simpler depreciation rules for small business](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/income-deductions-and-concessions/depreciation-and-capital-expenses-and-allowances/simpler-depreciation-for-small-business) - [Prime cost (straight line) and diminishing value methods](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/income-deductions-and-concessions/depreciation-and-capital-expenses-and-allowances/general-depreciation-rules-capital-allowances/prime-cost-straight-line-and-diminishing-value-methods) ## Software development pools You can allocate expenses you incur for the development of in-house software, which you intend to use solely for income producing purposes, to a software development pool. This includes expenses incurred before the in-house software is installed and ready for use. Once you make the choice to allocate these expenses to a software development pool, you must allocate all later in-house software expenses to a pool. A different pool is created for each income year in which you incur development expenses. In-house software that is allocated to a software development pool is depreciated at the following rates: - For expenditure incurred from 1 July 2015 Year 1 – Nil Year 2 – 30% Year 3 – 30% Year 4 – 30% Year 5 – 10% - For expenditure incurred up to 30 June 2015 Year 1 – Nil Year 2 – 40% Year 3 – 40% Year 4 – 20% If you’re entitled to claim a GST input tax credit for the expense, the amount allocated to the software development pool does not include the credit. ## Disposal of in-house software If you have allocated software development expenses from a project to a software development pool and the project is abandoned, the amounts remain part of the pool. If you receive consideration for software in a software development pool, you must include the consideration in your assessable income unless you choose rollover relief to apply. An example of consideration would be insurance proceeds on the destruction of the software. If you stop using in-house software that has not been allocated to a software development pool and you never expect to use it again, you can claim an immediate deduction for the cost of the software at that time. You can also claim an immediate deduction for expenses on in-house software that have not been allocated to a software development pool if you: - haven’t used the software and decide that you will never use it - had it installed ready for use and decide that you will never use it. The amount you can deduct is your total expenses for the software less any amount you receive for the software (or a part of it). **See also:** - [Disposing or ceasing to use a depreciating asset](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/income-deductions-and-concessions/depreciation-and-capital-expenses-and-allowances/general-depreciation-rules-capital-allowances/disposing-or-ceasing-to-use-a-depreciating-asset) - [Rollover relief](https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/depreciating-assets-guide-2015/what-happens-if-you-no-longer-hold-or-use-a-depreciating-asset?anchor=Rollover_relief#Rollover_relief) Expenses for in-house software may be deducted in a number of different ways depending on the circumstances. SECT 26.10 **Leave payments** (1) You cannot deduct [under](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#under) [this Act](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#this_act) a loss or outgoing for long service leave, annual leave, sick leave or other leave except: (a) an amount paid in the [income year](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_year) to the [individual](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#individual) to whom the leave relates (or, if that [individual](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#individual) has died, to that [individual](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#individual)'s dependant or \\* [legal personal representative](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#legal_personal_representative)); or (b) an \\* accrued leave transfer [payment](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#payment) that is made in the [income year](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_year). (2) An accrued leave transfer [payment](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#payment)is a [payment](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#payment) that an entity [makes](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#make): (a) in respect of an [individual](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#individual)'s leave (some or all of [which](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.5.html#which) accrued while the entity was required to [make](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#make) [payments](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#payment) in respect of the [individual](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#individual)'s leave, or leave the [individual](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#individual) might take); and (b) when the entity is no longer required (or is about to stop being required) to [make](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#make) [payments](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#payment) in respect of such leave; and (c) to another entity when the other entity has begun (or is about to begin) to be required to [make](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#make) [payments](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#payment) in respect of such leave; and (d) [under](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#under) (or for the purposes of facilitating the provisions of) an \\* Australian law, or an award, order, determination or industrial agreement [under](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#under) an \\* Australian law. It does not matter whether the leave accrues to the [individual](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#individual) as an employee or for some other reason. Example: Your employee goes to a new employer. You pay the new employer $2,000 for the employee's unused long service leave because an industrial agreement requires you to [make](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#make) that [payment](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#payment). Note: An accrued leave transfer [payment](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#payment) is included in the assessable income of the entity to [which](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.5.html#which) it is made: see section 15 \- 5\. * * * **AustLII:** [Copyright Policy](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/austlii/copyright.html) **\|** [Disclaimers](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/austlii/disclaimers.html) **\|** [Privacy Policy](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/austlii/privacy.html) **\|** [Feedback](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/austlii/feedback.html)

Legal expenses - to establish rights to intellectual property", "DC.Identifier": "AID/AID20021081", "title": "ATO ID 2002/1081 | Legal database", "dc.Date.ValidFromF": "2014-06-20", "dc.Language": "en-au", "dc.Rights": "http://www.ato.gov.au/content/corporate/about_this_site.htm#copyright", "dc.Audience": "all", "dc.Date.Modified": "", "dc.Publisher": "Australian Taxation Office", "ato.stylesheet": "CDS", "language": "en-au", "DC.Coverage.PlaceNAME.Area": "Australia", "viewport": "width=device-width, initial-scale=1, maximum-scale=1, user-scalable=no", "ato.Keywords": "Intellectual property rights;Legal expenses;Ownership, interests, control & rights", "DC.Subject": "ATO ID", "DC.Creator": "Australian Taxation Office", "FSM.Security": "Public", "DC.Format": "HTML", "ato.reference.id": "AID/AID20021081", "dc.Date.ValidToF": "indefinite", "favicon": "https://www.ato.gov.au/favicon.ico", "scrapeId": "01a0e5d3-289c-7292-99bd-a100e40ee992", "sourceURL": "https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/print?DocID=AID%2FAID20021081%2F00001&PiT=99991231235958", "url": "https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/print?DocID=AID%2FAID20021081%2F00001&PiT=99991231235958", "statusCode": 200, "contentType": "text/html", "timezone": "America/New_York", "proxyUsed": "basic", "cacheState": "miss", "indexId": "21776b50-d600-4e0b-868a-fb44ee7dfabe", "creditsUsed": 5, "concurrencyLimited": false }, "answer": "The issue is whether the taxpayer is entitled to a deduction under section 8-1 of the Income Tax Assessment Act 1997 for legal expenses incurred in establishing their rights in relation to written materials authored by them.\n\nThe decision is no, the taxpayer is not entitled to a deduction.\n\nRegarding *Herald and Weekly Times Ltd v FCT*, the document states: \"Legal expenses may be of a revenue nature and therefore deductible if they arise out of the day to day activities of the taxpayer's business or income producing activity (*Herald and Weekly Times Ltd v. The document does not mention deductibility of damages or settlement payments." }

    extract (page read): { "metadata": { "ato.reference.id": "TXR/TR9723/NAT/ATO/00001", "DCTERMS_description": "Income tax: deductions for repairs (Published on 3 December 1997)", "dc.Date.ValidFromF": "1997-12-03", "DC.Coverage.Placename.Area": "Australia", "dc.Language": "en-au", "FSM.Security": "Public", "viewport": "width=device-width, initial-scale=1, maximum-scale=1, user-scalable=no", "DC.Creator": "Australian Taxation Office", "ato.reference.natNumber": "97/9762-9", "robots": "index, nofollow", "DC.Format": "HTML", "dc.Date.Modified": "", "dc.Publisher": "Australian Taxation Office", "DC_TERMS_description": "Income tax: deductions for repairs (Published on 3 December 1997)", "DC.TERMS.description": "Income tax: deductions for repairs (Published on 3 December 1997)", "DC.Identifier": "TXR/TR9723/NAT/ATO", "server": "LDB5-3", "dc.Audience": "all", "dc.Date.Created": "1997/12/03", "dc.Rights": "http://www.ato.gov.au/content/corporate/about_this_site.htm#copyright", "DC.Title": "TR 97/23 - Income tax: deductions for repairs", "language": "en-au", "Keywords": "capital;entertainment;entirety;environmental protection expenditure;improvement;initial repairs;maintenance;notional repairs;reconstruction;renewal;renovation;repair;replacement;restoration", "DCTERMS.description": "Income tax: deductions for repairs (Published on 3 December 1997)", "title": "TR 97/23 | Legal database", "dc.Date.Issued": "1997/12/03", "dc.Date.ValidToF": "indefinite", "ato.Keywords": "capital;entertainment;entirety;environmental protection expenditure;improvement;initial repairs;maintenance;notional repairs;reconstruction;renewal;renovation;repair;replacement;restoration", "ato.stylesheet": "PBR", "DC.Subject": "ATO Ruling", "DC.Description": "Taxation Ruling", "description": "Taxation Ruling", "dc.Type.documentType": "ATO Ruling", "favicon": "https://www.ato.gov.au/favicon.ico", "scrapeId": "01a0e5d2-d682-76db-9168-4c5cad3931e5", "sourceURL": "https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?docid=TXR/TR9723/NAT/ATO/00001", "url": "https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?docid=TXR/TR9723/NAT/ATO/00001", "statusCode": 200, "contentType": "text/html", "proxyUsed": "basic", "cacheState": "hit", "cachedAt": "2026-09-28T02:19:11.091Z", "creditsUsed": 5, "concurrencyLimited": false }, "answer": "Paragraph 59 states: \"Expenditure incurred on an initial repair after property is acquired, if the expenditure is incurred in remedying defects, damage or deterioration in existence at the date of acquisition, is capital expenditure and is not, therefore, deductible under section 25-10.\"\n\nParagraph 61 states: \"It is immaterial whether at the time of acquisition the taxpayer was aware of the condition of the property, including its need for repair. It is also immaterial whether the purchase price (or lease rentals) reflected the need for repairs. We consider that the English Court of Appeal decision in _Odeon Associated Theatres Ltd v Jones (Inspector of Taxes)_ [1972] 1 All ER 681 is not authority in Australia for a contrary view. An initial repair expense is not the type of repair expenditure ordinarily incurred as a working or operating expense in producing assessable income or in carrying on a business. This is because it lacks a connection with the conduct or operations of the taxpayer that produce the taxpayer's assessable income. It is essentially an additional cost of acquiring the property or an improvement in the quality of the property acquired. Initial repair expenditure relates to the establishment of the profit - yielding structure. It is capital expenditure and is not deductible under section 25-10.\"\n\nParagraph 126 states: \"The leading Australian case in this area is the High Court decision in the _Thomas_ case. There, Windeyer J held that the costs of repairing a roof, guttering, wall, basement floor and wooden floor and painting a building in the year of income it was acquired was expenditure of a capital nature.\"\n\nParagraph 127 states: \"His Honour said (at 115 CLR 72; 14 ATD 87): 'Expenditure upon repairs is properly attributable to revenue account when the repairs are for the maintenance of an income-producing capital asset. Maintenance involves the periodic repair of defects that are the result of normal wear and tear in operation. It is an expense of a revenue nature when it is to repair defects arising from the operations of the person who incurs it. **But if when a thing is bought for use as a capital asset in the buyer's business it is not in good order and suitable for use in the way intended, the cost of putting it in order suitable for use is part of the cost of its acquisition, not a cost of its maintenance**. The decision of the Court of Session in _Law Shipping Co. Ltd. v. Inland Revenue Commissioners,_ \\[(1923) 12 TC 621\\] is commonly cited as authority for that proposition. The principle is obvious without the need for any supporting authority.'\"" }

or (ii) section [355](http://www.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s355.html)\- 205 (R&D expenditure) or 355 \- 480 (earlier year [associate](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s128fa.html#associate) R&D expenditure); of the [Income Tax Assessment Act 1997](http://www.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/); and (b) the requirements in [subsections](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s79a.html#subsection)(2), (3), (4) and (5) are met. (2A) A [taxpayer](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#taxpayer) is covered by this [subsection](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s79a.html#subsection) for the expenditure year if: (a) the [taxpayer](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#taxpayer) is not a [small business entity](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#small_business_entity) for the expenditure year; and (b) the [taxpayer](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#taxpayer) would be a [small business entity](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#small_business_entity) for the expenditure year if: (i) each reference in Subdivision 328 \- C (about what is a [small business entity](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#small_business_entity)) of the [Income Tax Assessment Act 1997](http://www.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/)to $10 million were instead a reference to $50 million; and (ii) the reference in [paragraph](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s79a.html#paragraph)328 \- 110(5)(b) of that Act to a [small business entity](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#small_business_entity) were instead a reference to a [taxpayer](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#taxpayer) covered by this [subsection](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s79a.html#subsection). (3) The expenditure must be: (a) either: (i) incurred in carrying on a [business](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#business); or (ii) incurred otherwise than in carrying on a [business](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#business) by a [taxpayer](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#taxpayer) that is not an individual; and (b) incurred under an agreement (see [subsection](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s79a.html#subsection)82KZL(1); and (c) incurred in [return](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#return) for the doing of a thing under the agreement that is not to be wholly done within the expenditure year. Requirement for expenditure not to meet pre \- RBT obligation (5) The expenditure must not meet a pre \- RBT obligation (see [subsection](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s79a.html#subsection)82KZL(1)). Relationship with other provisions (6) Section [82KZMD](http://www.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s82kzmd.html) has effect: (a) despite section 8 \- 1 of the [Income Tax Assessment Act 1997](http://www.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/); and (b) subject to Division 245 of that Act. * * * **AustLII:** [Copyright Policy](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/austlii/copyright.html) **\|** [Disclaimers](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/austlii/disclaimers.html) **\|** [Privacy Policy](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/austlii/privacy.html) **\|** [Feedback](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/austlii/feedback.html)

    extract (page read): ## [![](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/images/tiny-austlii.gif)](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/) Commonwealth Consolidated Acts \[ [Index](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/)\] \[ [Table](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/index.html#s25.25)\] \[ [Search](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/sinoform.pl)\] \[ [Search this Act](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/sinoform.pl/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/)\] \[ [Notes](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/notes.html)\] \[ [Noteup](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/sinosrch.pl?query=cth+consol_act+itaa1997240+s25.25)\] \[ [Previous](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s25.20.html)\] \[ [Next](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s25.30.html)\] \[ [Download](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/download.cgi/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240)\] \[ [Help](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/help/legis-help.html)\] * * * ### INCOME TAX ASSESSMENT ACT 1997 - SECT 25.25 **Borrowing expenses** (1) You can deduct expenditure you incur for \\* borrowing [money](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#money), to the extent that you use the [money](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#money) for the \* [purpose of producing assessable income](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#purpose_of_producing_assessable_income). In most [cases](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.5.html#cases) the [deduction](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.15.html#deduction) is spread [over](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#over) the \\* [period of the loan](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#period_of_the_loan). For the [cases](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.5.html#cases) where the [deduction](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.15.html#deduction) is not spread, see [subsection](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s26.97.html#subsection)(6). Note: Your [deductions](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.15.html#deduction) [under](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#under) this section may be reduced if any of your commercial debts have been [forgiven](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#forgive) in the [income year](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_year): see Subdivision 245 \- E. [Income year](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_year) when [money](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#money) used solely for the [purpose of producing assessable income](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#purpose_of_producing_assessable_income) (2) You can deduct for an [income year](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_year) the maximum amount worked out [under](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#under) [subsection](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s26.97.html#subsection)(4) if you use the \\* borrowed [money](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#money) during that [income year](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_year)solely for the \\* [purpose of producing assessable income](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#purpose_of_producing_assessable_income). Example: In 1997 \- 98 you borrow $100,000 and incur expenditure of $1,500 for the borrowing. You use the [money](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#money) to buy a house. Throughout 1998 - 99 you rent the house to a tenant. You can deduct for the expenditure for 1998 \- 99 the maximum amount worked out [under](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#under) [subsection](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s26.97.html#subsection)(4). [Income year](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_year) when borrowed [money](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#money) used [partly](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#part) for that purpose (3) If you use the [money](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#money) only [partly](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#part)for that purpose during that [income year](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_year), you can deduct the proportion of that maximum amount that is appropriate having regard to the extent that you used the \\* borrowed [money](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#money) for that purpose. Note: You cannot deduct anything for that [income year](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_year) if you do not use the [money](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#money) for that purpose at all during that [income year](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_year). Maximum [deduction](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.15.html#deduction) for an [income year](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_year) (4) You work out as follows the maximum amount that you can deduct for the expenditure for an [income year](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_year): [Method](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.15.html#method) statement Step 1. Work out the remaining expenditure as follows: • For the [income year](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_year) in [which](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.5.html#which) the \\* [period of the loan](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#period_of_the_loan) begins, it is the amount of the expenditure. • For a later [income year](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_year), it is the amount of the expenditure reduced by the maximum amount that you can deduct for the expenditure for [each](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.15.html#each) earlier [income year](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_year). Step 2. Work out the remaining loan period as follows: • For the [income year](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_year) in [which](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.5.html#which) the \\* [period of the loan](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#period_of_the_loan) begins, it is the [period of the loan](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#period_of_the_loan) (as determined at the end of the [income year](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_year)). • For a later [income year](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_year), it is the period from the start of the [income year](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_year) until the end of the [period of the loan](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#period_of_the_loan) (as determined at the end of the [income year](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_year)). Step 3. Divide the remaining expenditure by the number of days in the remaining loan period. Step 4. Multiply the result from Step 3 by the number of days in the remaining loan period that are in the [income year](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_year). Example: To continue the example in [subsection](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s26.97.html#subsection)(2): suppose the original [period of the loan](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#period_of_the_loan) is 4 years starting on 1 September 1997. What is the maximum amount you can deduct for the expenditure for 1997 \- 98? Applying the [method](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.15.html#method) statement: After Step 1: the remaining expenditure is $1,500 (the amount of the expenditure). After Step 2: the remaining loan period is 4 years from 1 September 1997 (1,461 days). After Step 3: the result is $1,500 divided by 1,461 = $1.03. After Step 4: the result is $1.03 multiplied by 302 days = $310.06. Suppose you repay the loan early, on 31 December 1998. What is the maximum amount you can deduct for the expenditure for 1998 \- 99? Applying the [method](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.15.html#method) statement: After Step 1: the remaining expenditure is $1,500 (the amount of the expenditure) reduced by $310.06 (the maximum amount you can deduct for 1997 - 98) = $1,189.94. After Step 2: the remaining loan period is the period from 1 July 1998 to 31 December 1998 (183 days). After Step 3: the result is $1,189.94 divided by 183 days = $6.50. After Step 4: the result is $6.50 multiplied by 183 days = $1,189.94. But this exception does not apply to the extent that the taxable [value](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.15.html#value) of the \\* [fringe benefit](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#fringe_benefit) is reduced [under](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#under) section [63A](http://www.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/fbtaa1986312/s63a.html) of the [Fringe Benefits Tax Assessment Act 1986](http://www.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/fbtaa1986312/). Note 1: You may be able to deduct losses or outgoings that are [fringe benefits](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#fringe_benefit) [under](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#under) section [51AEA](http://www.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s51aea.html), [51AEB](http://www.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s51aeb.html) or [51AEC](http://www.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s51aec.html) of the [Income Tax Assessment Act 1936](http://www.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/). If you do, then you cannot deduct them [under](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#under) section 8 \- 1 (about [general deductions](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#general_deduction)) and so this section is not relevant.     extract (page read): [Skip to main content](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/hiring-and-paying-your-workers/fringe-benefits-tax/types-of-fringe-benefits/entertainment-related-fringe-benefits/common-entertainment-scenarios-for-business#content) [Skip To search](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/hiring-and-paying-your-workers/fringe-benefits-tax/types-of-fringe-benefits/entertainment-related-fringe-benefits/common-entertainment-scenarios-for-business#search-box) [Skip To Alex Virtual Assistant](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/hiring-and-paying-your-workers/fringe-benefits-tax/types-of-fringe-benefits/entertainment-related-fringe-benefits/common-entertainment-scenarios-for-business#alex-virtual-assistant) # Common entertainment scenarios for business Examples of how FBT applies to businesses for Christmas parties, recreation days, seminars and other events. **Last updated** 12 January 2023 Print or Download ## On this page - [Christmas parties and gifts](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/hiring-and-paying-your-workers/fringe-benefits-tax/types-of-fringe-benefits/entertainment-related-fringe-benefits/common-entertainment-scenarios-for-business#ato-Christmaspartiesandgifts) - [Gym membership](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/hiring-and-paying-your-workers/fringe-benefits-tax/types-of-fringe-benefits/entertainment-related-fringe-benefits/common-entertainment-scenarios-for-business#ato-Gymmembership) - [Holiday](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/hiring-and-paying-your-workers/fringe-benefits-tax/types-of-fringe-benefits/entertainment-related-fringe-benefits/common-entertainment-scenarios-for-business#ato-Holiday) - [Golf day](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/hiring-and-paying-your-workers/fringe-benefits-tax/types-of-fringe-benefits/entertainment-related-fringe-benefits/common-entertainment-scenarios-for-business#ato-Golfday) - [Afternoon tea](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/hiring-and-paying-your-workers/fringe-benefits-tax/types-of-fringe-benefits/entertainment-related-fringe-benefits/common-entertainment-scenarios-for-business#ato-Afternoontea) - [Seminars](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/hiring-and-paying-your-workers/fringe-benefits-tax/types-of-fringe-benefits/entertainment-related-fringe-benefits/common-entertainment-scenarios-for-business#ato-Seminars) These scenarios apply to commercial businesses. There are [different scenarios for income tax exempt bodies](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/hiring-and-paying-your-workers/fringe-benefits-tax/types-of-fringe-benefits/entertainment-related-fringe-benefits/fbt-and-entertainment-for-not-for-profit-and-government-organisations/common-entertainment-scenarios-for-income-tax-exempt-bodies). ## Christmas parties and gifts If your business holds a Christmas party: - on a working day, on your business premises, and only for your current employees, you don’t pay fringe benefits tax (FBT) for the food and drink - off your business premises, or the party includes associates of employees (such as their partners), you don't pay FBT if the party is a [minor benefit](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/hiring-and-paying-your-workers/fringe-benefits-tax/exemptions-concessions-and-other-ways-to-reduce-fbt/minor-benefits-exemption) – that is, the cost for each person is less than $300 and it would be considered unreasonable to treat it as a fringe benefit - that includes clients, you don't pay FBT for the costs relating to the clients. If you give your employees a Christmas gift, you don't pay FBT if the value of the gift is less than $300 per person and it would be considered unreasonable to treat it as a fringe benefit. If the Christmas party is not subject to FBT, you can't claim income tax deductions for the cost of the party. **Example: Christmas party on business premises** A company holds a Christmas lunch on its business premises on a working day. - Employees, their partners and clients attend. - The company provides food and drink, and taxi travel home. - The cost per head is $125. **Entertainment is being provided** A party for employees, associates and clients is entertainment, because the purpose of the function is for the people attending to enjoy themselves. **Employees – no FBT, exemption applies** The employer doesn't pay FBT for the: - food and drink for employees, because it is provided and consumed on a working day on the business premises - taxi travel, because there is a specific FBT exemption for taxi travel directly to or from the workplace. **Associates – no FBT, exemption applies** The employer doesn't pay FBT for the food, drink and taxi travel provided to the employees' partners (associates), because it is a [minor benefit](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/hiring-and-paying-your-workers/fringe-benefits-tax/exemptions-concessions-and-other-ways-to-reduce-fbt/minor-benefits-exemption) – that is, it has a value of less than $300 and it would be unreasonable to treat it as a fringe benefit. **Clients – no FBT** There is no FBT on benefits provided to clients. **Income tax and GST credits** The employer can't claim an income tax deduction or GST credits for the food, drink or taxi travel provided for employees, associates or clients. End of example ## Gym membership **Example: gym membership** A conveyancing firm pays for a one-year gym membership for the company's director and each employee. The cost is $480 per person. **Entertainment is being provided** The gym membership is recreation entertainment. **Employees – FBT applies** FBT applies to the gym memberships for the employees. The minor benefits exemption doesn't apply, because the cost of the gym membership is $300 or more. **Director – FBT applies** The director is an employee of the company. Therefore FBT applies to the gym membership for the director. **Income tax and GST credits** The employer can claim: - an income tax deduction and GST credits for the cost of the gym memberships - an income tax deduction for the FBT paid. End of example ## Holiday **Example: holiday given as reward** A computer manufacturer offers a reward to employees of a retail computer store. - The retailer agrees that the manufacturer can offer the reward to its employees. - If an employee sells 200 computers in a month, they will receive a holiday consisting of 2 nights' accommodation at the beach and 2 tickets to an aquarium. - The total value of each holiday package is $600. **Entertainment is being provided** - The holiday and tickets to the aquarium are recreation entertainment. **Employees – FBT applies** - FBT applies to the accommodation and tickets given to the employees who meet the sales target. The minor benefits exemption doesn't apply, because the value of the holiday package is $300 or more. **FBT liability – retailer** - The retailer, as the employer, is liable to pay the FBT as the benefits are being provided under an agreement with the manufacturer. **Income tax and GST credits** - The retailer can claim an income tax deduction for the FBT they pay. - The manufacturer can claim an income tax deduction and GST credits for the cost of purchasing the accommodation and tickets. End of example ## Golf day **Example: golf day for employees, associates and clients** Paul, an employee, takes several clients and his partner to a corporate golf day paid for by his employer. - The event is not held on a working day. - Paul's employer gives him taxi vouchers to go from his home to pick up his clients and take them back after the event. - The total cost is $320 per person. **Entertainment is being provided** The golf day is recreation entertainment. It is a social event and the purpose is for people to enjoy themselves. **Employees – FBT applies** FBT applies to the food, drink and taxi travel provided to Paul. - The minor benefit exemption doesn't apply because the cost per person is $300 or more. - The taxi travel exemption doesn't apply because Paul's trip did not begin or end at the workplace. **Associates – FBT applies** FBT applies to the food, drink and taxi travel provided to Paul's partner. **Clients – no FBT** There is no FBT on the food, drink, and taxi travel provided to clients. **Income tax and GST credits** The employer: - can claim an income tax deduction and GST credits for the cost of providing the fringe benefits to the employee and his associate - can claim an income tax deduction for any FBT paid - can't claim an income tax deduction or GST credits for the entertainment provided to the clients. End of example ## Afternoon tea **Example: celebration afternoon tea on business premises** Anjelica is getting married. To celebrate, her company hosts an informal event on the business premises with drinks and finger food, and invites Anjelica's associates, work colleagues and clients. The cost is $25 per person. **Entertainment is being provided** The informal event is a social event and is therefore entertainment. **Employees – no FBT, exemption applies** Food and drink is exempt from FBT when consumed by employees on business premises on a working day. **Associates – no FBT, exemption applies** The food and drink provided to Anjelica's associates is exempt from FBT because it is a [minor benefit](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/hiring-and-paying-your-workers/fringe-benefits-tax/exemptions-concessions-and-other-ways-to-reduce-fbt/minor-benefits-exemption) – that is, it cost less than $300 per employee and it would be considered unreasonable to treat the benefit as a fringe benefit. **Clients – no FBT** There is no FBT on benefits provided to clients. **Income tax and GST credits** The employer can't claim an income tax deduction or GST credits for food or drink provided to the employees, their associates or clients. End of example ## Seminars The 'otherwise deductible' rule may apply to food or drink provided at seminars. This means you (as the employer) do not pay FBT on an expense your employee could have claimed as a deduction, had they paid for it themselves. The otherwise deductible rule works like this: - If the food or drink at a seminar does not amount to entertainment - then the registration fee would have been deductible in full and the employer does not pay FBT. - If the food or drink at a seminar does amount to entertainment, and - is reasonably incidental to the employee attending a seminar that goes for at least 4 hours – the registration fee is deductible and the employer does not pay FBT - is not reasonably incidental to the employee attending a seminar that goes for at least 4 hours – only that proportion of the registration fee that does not relate to the food or drink would have been deductible, and the employer is liable to pay FBT on the remainder. ### Meaning of 'seminar' A seminar is: - any training session, including a conference, convention, lecture, meeting, speech, question and answer session or educational course - a planning day - at which employees discuss general policy issues relevant to the management of your business - conducted at an external premises available for conferences, training or seminars - not a business meeting, where the main purpose of the meeting is to give or receive information, or discuss matters relating to the organisation - not a marketing presentation, where the main purpose is to promote a business (or prospective business) or its products and services. ### Meaning of 'reasonably incidental' Food or drink is reasonably incidental to a seminar if it is: - provided for sustenance because of the duration, time of day or location of the seminar - provided immediately before, during or immediately following working sessions of the seminar - available to all participants. ### Duration of at least 4 hours For the purposes of the otherwise deductible rule, the seminar must go for at least 4 hours. The 4-hour period does not include any part of the seminar that occurs during a meal, or any breaks during the seminar for meals, rest or recreation. **Example: business planning day** An insurance company organises a planning day for its managers at a conference centre. The company provides morning and afternoon tea and a 3-course lunch (excluding alcohol) at a cost of $125 per head. **Entertainment** The morning and afternoon tea are light meals and not considered entertainment. The 3-course lunch would be elaborate and therefore considered to be entertainment, even though it is work related. **Employees – no FBT, exemption applies** The company doesn't pay FBT for the seminar, including the 3-course lunch, because it is a [minor benefit](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/hiring-and-paying-your-workers/fringe-benefits-tax/exemptions-concessions-and-other-ways-to-reduce-fbt/minor-benefits-exemption) – that is, it has a value of less than $300 and it would be considered unreasonable to treat it as a fringe benefit. **Income tax and GST credits** The lunch is entertainment and is exempt from FBT under the minor benefits exemption. Therefore the employer can't claim an income tax deduction or GST credits for the lunch. The employer can claim a deduction for the morning and afternoon teas, which are not entertainment. The employer will need to determine how much of the $125 cost is attributable to the morning and afternoon teas. End of example Examples of how FBT applies to businesses for Christmas parties, recreation days, seminars and other events. QC71139 Print or Download

[[18]] INCOME TAX ASSESSMENT ACT 1997 - SECT 36.17 How to deduct tax losses of corporate tax entities — https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s36.17.html
    extract (page read): ## [![](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/images/tiny-austlii.gif)](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/) Commonwealth Consolidated Acts \[ [Index](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/)\] \[ [Table](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/index.html#s36.17)\] \[ [Search](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/sinoform.pl)\] \[ [Search this Act](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/sinoform.pl/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/)\] \[ [Notes](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/notes.html)\] \[ [Noteup](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/sinosrch.pl?query=cth+consol_act+itaa1997240+s36.17)\] \[ [Previous](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s36.15.html)\] \[ [Next](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s36.20.html)\] \[ [Download](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/download.cgi/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240)\] \[ [Help](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/help/legis-help.html)\] * * * ### INCOME TAX ASSESSMENT ACT 1997 - SECT 36.17 **How to deduct tax losses of corporate tax entities** (1) A \\* [tax loss](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#tax_loss) of an entity for a \\* [loss year](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#loss_year) is deducted in a later [income year](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_year) as follows if the entity is a \\* corporate tax entity at any time during the later [income year](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_year). Note 1: A [tax loss](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#tax_loss) can be deducted [under](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#under) this section only to the extent that it has not already been [utilised](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#utilise): see [subsection](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s40.105.html#subsection)960 - 20(1). Note 2: A corporate tax entity may also, in the 2020 \- 21, 2021 \- 22 or 2022 \- 23 [income year](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_year), be able to carry a loss back to the 2018 \- 19, 2019 - 20, 2020 \- 21 or 2021 \- 2022 [income year](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_year): see Division 160\. If the entity has no [net exempt income](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#net_exempt_income) (2) If the entity's total assessable income for the later [income year](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_year) exceeds the entity's total [deductions](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.15.html#deduction) (except \\* [tax losses](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#tax_loss)), the entity is to deduct from that excess so much of the [tax loss](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#tax_loss) as the entity chooses. The entity may choose a nil amount. If the entity has [net exempt income](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#net_exempt_income) (3) If the entity has \\* [net exempt income](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#net_exempt_income) for the later [income year](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_year) and the entity's total assessable income (if any) for that year exceeds the entity's total [deductions](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.15.html#deduction) (except \\* [tax losses](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#tax_loss)), the entity is to: (a) first, deduct the [tax loss](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#tax_loss) from the [net exempt income](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#net_exempt_income); and (b) secondly, deduct from the [part](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#part) of the total assessable income that exceeds those [deductions](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.15.html#deduction) so much of the undeducted amount of the [tax loss](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#tax_loss) (if any) as the entity chooses. The entity may choose a nil amount [under](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#under) [paragraph](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s40.140.html#paragraph)(b). Note: To work out the corporate tax entity's [net exempt income](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#net_exempt_income): see section 36 \- 20\. (4) However, if the entity has \\* [net exempt income](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#net_exempt_income) for the later [income year](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_year) and those [deductions](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.15.html#deduction) exceed the entity's total assessable income, the entity is to: (a) subtract that excess from the [net exempt income](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#net_exempt_income); and (b) deduct the \\* [tax loss](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#tax_loss) from any [net exempt income](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#net_exempt_income) that remains. Note: This means there is no choice available [under](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#under) this [subsection](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s40.105.html#subsection). (4A) For [subsection](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s40.105.html#subsection)(3) or (4), if the entity has \* exempt income [under](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#under) section [51](http://www.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s51.html)\- 100 (about shipping) for the later [income year](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_year), disregard 90% of so much of the entity's \\* [net exempt income](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#net_exempt_income) for the later [income year](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_year) as directly relates to that exempt income. Limit to how much the entity can choose (5) The choice that the entity has [under](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#under) [subsection](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s40.105.html#subsection)(2) or (3) for the later [income year](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_year) is subject to both of the following: (a) the entity [must](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.15.html#must) choose a nil amount if, disregarding the \* [tax loss](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#tax_loss) and other [tax losses](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#tax_loss) of the entity, the entity would have an amount of \\* excess franking offsets for that year; (b) if, disregarding the [tax loss](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#tax_loss) and other [tax losses](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#tax_loss) of the entity, the entity would not have an amount of excess franking offsets for that year--the entity [must](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.15.html#must) not choose an amount that would result in the entity having an amount of excess franking offsets for that year. Example: For the 2017 \- 18 [income year](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_year), Company A (which is not a base rate entity) has: - a [tax loss](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#tax_loss) of $150 from a previous [income year](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_year); and - assessable income of $200 (franked distribution of $70, [franking credit](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#franking_credit) of $30 and $100 of income from other sources); and - no [deductions](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.15.html#deduction); and - no [net exempt income](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#net_exempt_income). The [tax offset](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#tax_offset) of $30 from the [franking credit](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#franking_credit) is not stated in Division 67 to be subject to the refundable [tax offset](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#tax_offset) rules. Company A would not have an amount of excess franking offsets for that year if the [tax loss](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#tax_loss) were disregarded (see section 36 \- [55](http://www.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s55.html)). [Paragraph](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s40.140.html#paragraph)(a) therefore does not apply. correctness.justification: The headline answer contradicts the reference on two material figures: it leads with the full $45,000 interest deduction (reference: $6,159 = $45,000 × 150/1,096) and adds $5,000 for initial repairs via temporary full expensing (reference: nil under s 25-10, capital allowances merely flagged), producing $81,842 + $50,000 against the reference's $88,001 total; the correct $6,159 appears only as a buried alternative and the 'textbook view $50,335' matches neither the reference's $38,001 (ex-loss) nor $88,001. The remaining ten items match the reference exactly with correct provisions (s 26-10, s 25-5, s 25-10, s 28-10, s 25-25 $342, Div 32, Div 30, dividends nil, $50,000 loss under s 36-17 with COT met), so the error is material but confined.

completeness.justification: Every reference point is covered: provision vs paid leave, both legal/damages amounts with the capital and penalty exclusions addressed, s 25-5 with the capital proviso, the repairs split with initial repairs capital, company car free of Div 28, interest with the 150/1,096 apportionment shown, borrowing expenses at $342 with the leap-year day count, entertainment denied, gift with the s 26-55 limit added, dividends, and the $50,000 loss with continuity of ownership. The leading authority on initial repairs (W Thomas & Co, via TR 97/23) is engaged with Windeyer J's operative passage quoted, plus extras (s 70-10/70-35 trading stock, minor-benefit analysis, TFE) beyond the reference; no research-process narration.

faithfulness.justification: Roughly 80-85% of load-bearing claims are anchored at the claim and verified from captured text, with governing statutory words captured verbatim for ss 26-10, 25-5, 25-10, 40-190, 28-10, 70-10, 82KZM(1)/(1A), 82KZMA, 82KZMD, 25-25, 32-20, 26-55, 165-12 and 36-17. Unverified items: s 8-1's words are never captured despite underpinning the legal, car, interest and dividend claims; the s 30-15 gift deduction rule is cited but uncaptured; the claim that Herald & Weekly Times allowed damages is expressly not borne out by the ATO ID capture ('The document does not mention deductibility of damages or settlement payments'); FCT v St Hubert's Island is named without capture; and the TFE proposition rests solely on an ATO web page.

helpfulness.justification: The answer has the working elements of professional advice: verbatim statutory text, day-count computations shown ($45,000 × 150/1,096; $2,500 × 150/1,096), a summary table, and a concrete closing list of facts to confirm (turnover, prepayment period, asset acquisition dates, party attendees, assessable income, s 70-35 adjustment). It loses polish by leading with an assumption-dependent headline total and three competing figures, and by mislabelling its $50,335 scenario as the 'textbook view' when the expected textbook computation is the $6,159 apportionment it presents only as a third scenario.

citation_grounding.justification: Citations are densely anchored at the claim (e.g. '(s 26-10 [[1]])', 's 25-25(4)-(5) [[13]]') and mostly verified from captured primary legislation, including the full s 82KZM(1A) medium-business text and the s 25-25 method statement; TR 97/23's capture supplies the actual W Thomas passage and the ATO entertainment page verifies the Christmas-party outcome. A small minority is unverified or secondary-only: s 8-1 and s 30-15 are cited with no captured text anywhere, TFE deductibility is grounded only in ATO guidance rather than Subdiv 40-BB, the damages sub-claim is unsupported by the ATO ID capture, and St Hubert's Island is uncaptured.

judge_output.summary: Meticulously sourced and complete answer whose primary bottom line is wrong against the reference (interest claimed in full at $45,000 and $5,000 TFE for initial repairs versus the reference's $6,159 and nil), though the reference figures and analysis are all present as alternatives.
