    extract (page read): - [**All Databases**](https://www.austlii.edu.au/databases.html) - [**Cases & Legislation**](https://www.austlii.edu.au/databases.html) - [**Journals & Scholarship**](https://www.austlii.edu.au/au/journals/) - [**Law Reform**](https://www.austlii.edu.au/au/special/lawreform/) - [**Treaties**](https://www.austlii.edu.au/au/other/dfat/) - [**Libraries**](https://www.austlii.edu.au/database-libraries.html) - [**Communities**](http://austlii.community/wiki/) - [**LawCite**](https://www.austlii.edu.au/lawcite/) - [**Australia**](https://www.austlii.edu.au/databases.html) - [**CTH**](https://www.austlii.edu.au/au/cth/) - [**ACT**](https://www.austlii.edu.au/au/act/) - [**NSW**](https://www.austlii.edu.au/au/nsw/) - [**NT**](https://www.austlii.edu.au/au/nt/) - [**QLD**](https://www.austlii.edu.au/au/qld/) - [**SA**](https://www.austlii.edu.au/au/sa/) - [**TAS**](https://www.austlii.edu.au/au/tas/) - [**VIC**](https://www.austlii.edu.au/au/vic/) - [**WA**](https://www.austlii.edu.au/au/wa/) - [**New Zealand**](http://www.nzlii.org/databases.html) - ##### Specific Year [Any](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s25.5.html#) 2015 - [**Any**](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s25.5.html#) - ##### [Any](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/) # INCOME TAX ASSESSMENT ACT 1997 - SECT 25.5 Tax - related expenses ### INCOME TAX ASSESSMENT ACT 1997 - SECT 25.5 **Tax - related expenses** (1) You can deduct expenditure you incur to the extent that it is for: (a) managing your \\* [tax affairs](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#tax_affairs); or (b) complying with an obligation imposed on you by a \* Commonwealth law, insofar as that obligation relates to the \\* [tax affairs](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#tax_affairs) of an entity; or (ca) a [penalty](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s40.1035.html#penalty) [under](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#under) Subdivision 162 \- D of the \\* GST Act; or (cb) levy [under](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#under) the [Major Bank Levy Act 2017](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/num_act/mbla2017157/); or (d) obtaining a valuation in accordance with section 30 - 212 or 31 \- 15; or (e) managing your \\* Australian GloBE [tax affairs](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#tax_affairs); or (f) complying with an obligation imposed on you by a \* Commonwealth law, insofar as that obligation relates to the Australian GloBE [tax affairs](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#tax_affairs) of an entity. Note 1: To find out whether a [trustee](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#trustee) of a deceased estate can deduct expenditure [under](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#under) this section, see [subsection](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s26.97.html#subsection)69(7) of the [Income Tax Assessment Act 1936](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/). Note 2: If you receive an amount as [recoupment](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#recoupment) of the expenditure, the amount may be included in your assessable income: see Subdivision 20 - A. No [deduction](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.15.html#deduction) for certain expenditure (2) You cannot deduct [under](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#under) [subsection](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s26.97.html#subsection)(1): (a) \\* tax; or (b) an amount withheld or payable [under](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#under) [Part](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#part)2 \- 5 or [Part](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#part)2 \- 10 in Schedule 1 to the [Taxation Administration Act 1953](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/taa1953269/); or (c) expenditure for \\* borrowing [money](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#money) (including [payments](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#payment) of interest) to pay an amount [covered](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.5.html#cover) by [paragraph](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s26.85.html#paragraph)(a) or (b); or (d) expenditure for a matter relating to the commission (or possible commission) of an offence against an \\* Australian law or a \\* foreign law; or (e) a fee or commission for advice about the operation of a \* Commonwealth law relating to taxation, unless that advice is [provided](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#provide) by a \* [recognised tax adviser](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#recognised_tax_adviser). No [deduction](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.15.html#deduction) for expenditure excluded from [general deductions](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#general_deduction) (3) You cannot deduct expenditure [under](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#under) [subsection](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s26.97.html#subsection)(1) to the extent that a provision of [this Act](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#this_act) (except section 8 \- 1) expressly prevents or limits your deducting it [under](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#under) section 8 \- 1 (about [general deductions](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#general_deduction)). It does not matter whether the provision specifically refers to section 8 \- 1\. No [deduction](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.15.html#deduction) for capital expenditure (4) You cannot deduct capital expenditure [under](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#under) [subsection](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s26.97.html#subsection)(1). However, for this purpose, expenditure is not capital expenditure merely because the \\* [tax affairs](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#tax_affairs) or \\* Australian GloBE [tax affairs](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#tax_affairs) concerned relate to matters of a capital nature. Example: [Under](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#under) this section, you can deduct expenditure you incur in applying for a [private ruling](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#private_ruling) on whether you can depreciate an item of property. Use of property taken to be for income producing purpose (5) [Under](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#under) some provisions of [this Act](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#this_act) it is [important](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#import) to decide whether you used property for the \\* [purpose of producing assessable income](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#purpose_of_producing_assessable_income). For provisions of that kind, your use of property is taken to be for that purpose insofar as you use the property for: (a) managing your \\* [tax affairs](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#tax_affairs); or (b) complying with an obligation imposed on you by a \* Commonwealth law, insofar as that obligation relates to the \\* [tax affairs](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#tax_affairs) of another entity. Example: You buy a computer to prepare your tax [returns](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#return). The expenditure you incur in buying the computer is capital expenditure and cannot be deducted [under](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#under) this section. However, to the extent that you use the computer in preparing your [income tax return](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_tax_return), you [will](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.5.html#will) be able to deduct the decline in [value](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.15.html#value) of your computer [under](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#under) Division 40\. That is because, [under](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#under) this [subsection](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s26.97.html#subsection), the computer is property that you are taken to use for the [purpose of producing assessable income](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#purpose_of_producing_assessable_income). (6) If another provision of [this Act](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#this_act) expressly [provides](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#provide) that a [particular](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#part) use of property is not taken to be for the \* [purpose of producing assessable income](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#purpose_of_producing_assessable_income), that provision [overrides](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#over) [subsection](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s26.97.html#subsection)(5). Expenditure by [trustee](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#trustee) of deceased estate (8) If: (a) after you die, the [trustee](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#trustee) of your deceased estate incurs expenditure; and (b) had you incurred the expenditure before you died, you could have deducted it [under](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#under) [subsection](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s26.97.html#subsection)(1); for the purposes of assessing the [trustee](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#trustee) for the [income year](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_year) in [which](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.5.html#which) you died, the expenditure is a [deduction](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.15.html#deduction) [under](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#under) that [subsection](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s26.97.html#subsection). #### Navigate - completeness.justification: Substantively the answer covers everything in the reference and more — drawings excluded, stock excess under s 70-35(2), the 50% motor vehicle apportionment, the repair and accounting-fee treatments, the TR 2005/7 salary analysis with the split table, plus timing and insufficient-profits qualifications — but levels 4 and 5 each require no narration of the assistant's own research process, and the 'citing from memory as I did not reread it' and 'I haven't separately checked those provisions' statements are exactly that, capping the dimension at 3.

faithfulness.justification: The load-bearing claims are anchored at the claim and verified: the s 90 definition and s 92(1) inclusion rule ([[1]], [[2]], captured verbatim), the s 70-35(2) $8,000 excess ([[3]]), drawings/derivation independence and the TR 2005/7 salary treatment including paras 20-23 and the pre-year-end agreement requirement ([[4]], captured quotes), the logbook substantiation requirements ([[5]]), the s 25-10 repair deduction and capital exclusion ([[6]]) and s 25-5(1)(a) for accounting fees ([[7]]). Unanchored or unverified: deductibility of purchases and wages under s 8-1 (no citation, not captured), s 6-5 characterisation of sales and interest, the s 328-285 small business claim (expressly from memory) and the PAYG/SG assertion — a small minority, comfortably in the 75-94% band.

helpfulness.justification: Clear workings tables for (a)-(c), a statement of the governing framework, professional caveats (capital-vs-repair, logbook substantiation, small business stock rules) and an actionable timing point (salary agreement must be in place by 30 June 2023). Minor issues: the statutory words are paraphrased rather than set out in the prose, the 'from memory'/'haven't checked' disclosures are tone slips, and the PAYG/SG and s 328-285 asides sprawl beyond the question.

citation_grounding.justification: Claims are densely anchored at the claim to relevant authority whose captures verify them: full operative text of ss 90, 92(1), 70-35, 25-10(1)/(3), 25-5(1)(a) and 28-100, and extensive captured TR 2005/7 passages (salary not deductible, distribution of profits, s 92(1) allocation, advances, timing). A small minority of statutory propositions are ungrounded — s 8-1 for purchases and wages, s 6-5 for the income items, s 70-25, and the uncited s 328-285 and PAYG/SG claims — with no irrelevant or unsupportive citations, fitting level 4 rather than the 'every material claim' standard of level 5.

judge_output.summary: All figures and conclusions match the reference and the core rules are anchored to captured primary text (ss 90, 92(1), 70-35, 25-10, 25-5, 28-100, TR 2005/7), but a few minor claims run ahead of the sources (s 328-285 'from memory', PAYG/SG 'haven't checked') and the research-process disclosures cap Correctness and Completeness.

This publication is a public ruling for the purposes of the _Taxation Administration Act 1953._
This Ruling describes how the Commissioner will apply the law as amended by the [Tax Laws Amendment (Small Business Restructure Roll-over) Act 2016](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?DocID=PAC/20160018/ATOTOC) to entities that rely on this Ruling in good faith.
If you rely on this Ruling in good faith, you will not have to pay any underpaid tax, penalties or interest in respect of matters covered by the Ruling if it does not correctly state how a relevant provision applies to you. | **What this Ruling is about** 1\. This Ruling explains the income tax consequences and adjustments that occur when the transferor and transferee choose to apply the Small Business Restructure Roll-over (SBRR) in Subdivision 328-G of the _Income Tax Assessment Act 1997_ (ITAA 1997).[\[1\]](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?LocID=%22COG%2FLCR20162%2FNAT%2FATO%2Ffp1%22&PiT=99991231235958#fp1) 2\. The Ruling applies only where the requirements for the SBRR set out in section 328-430 are satisfied. We recommend reading this Ruling together with Law Companion Ruling LCR 2016/3 _Small Business Restructure Roll-over: genuine restructure of an ongoing business and related matters._ **Date of effect** 3\. This Ruling applies to transfers that occur on or after 1 July 2016 which involve: •a balancing adjustment event for a depreciating asset•trading stock or a revenue asset, or•a capital gains tax (CGT) event in respect of a CGT asset (that is not a depreciating asset, trading stock or revenue asset). **Background** 4\. The SBRR assists small business owners to undertake genuine restructures[\[2\]](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?LocID=%22COG%2FLCR20162%2FNAT%2FATO%2Ffp2%22&PiT=99991231235958#fp2) of their businesses which alter the way assets used in their businesses are held. 5\. The measure affects what gains or losses the transferor recognises, the carrying tax values for the transferee, and what subsequent losses on membership interests can be recognised. 5A. The SBRR does not affect other tax liabilities (for example, fringe benefits tax or goods and services tax), or prevent any liability for stamp duty from arising under State legislation. Existing obligations under other regulatory regimes, such as the corporations law, must still be complied with. Furthermore, care should be taken that any transactions involving a trust are within the power or duties of the trustee. The following examples are provided to illustrate these consequences. **_Example 1 - Restructure from company to discretionary trust_** _Facts_ 6\. Pep and Sally, a married couple, are the directors and shareholders in Vitamin Pty Ltd, which has issued two shares for total contributed capital of $100. Each share has a cost base of $50. Vitamin Pty Ltd carries on a naturopathy business. 7\. As at 1 January 2017, the active assets of the company are: •a small consulting room, which was acquired by Vitamin Pty Ltd for $200,000 in 2010 -no other additional capital expenditure has been outlaid in relation to the room-the market value is $230,000 •a pill press, with an adjustable value of $14,000•goodwill, which is self-generated, and•50 bottles of homeopathic pills, which were made and processed by Pep and Sally, and became Vitamin Pty Ltd's trading stock during the current income year at a cost of $250. 8\. The liabilities of the company, arising from a debt for unpaid income tax and trade creditors, total $24,000. 9\. A new discretionary trust, the P&S Trust, is settled and family trust election is made with Pep as the primary individual.[\[3\]](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?LocID=%22COG%2FLCR20162%2FNAT%2FATO%2Ffp3%22&PiT=99991231235958#fp3) 10\. On 1 January 2017, Pep and Sally cause Vitamin Pty Ltd to transfer all[\[4\]](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?LocID=%22COG%2FLCR20162%2FNAT%2FATO%2Ffp4%22&PiT=99991231235958#fp4) of its assets (except petty cash[\[4A\]](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?LocID=%22COG%2FLCR20162%2FNAT%2FATO%2Ffp4A%22&PiT=99991231235958#fp4A)) to the trustee of the P&S Trust (the trustee) in consideration for the trustee undertaking to discharge Vitamin Pty Ltd's liabilities. The company and the trustee choose to apply the SBRR. _No direct income tax consequences from the transfer of assets_ 11\. Under the SBRR, a transfer of an asset has no direct income tax consequences, except as provided for under Subdivision 328-G.[\[5\]](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?LocID=%22COG%2FLCR20162%2FNAT%2FATO%2Ffp5%22&PiT=99991231235958#fp5) Related roll-over relief for depreciating assets is available under section 40-340. Most importantly, this means: •No capital gain or loss arises from the transfer of the consulting room or goodwill.•No amount is included in Vitamin Pty Ltd's assessable income, or deduction allowed, as a result of a balancing adjustment event under Division 40 (capital allowances) for the transfer of the pill pressing machine.•As a result of the disposal of the pills to the trustee, Vitamin Pty Ltd is taken to have transferred the pills for their cost ($250) and not for their market value. Vitamin Pty Ltd includes $250 in its assessable income under section 70-90.[\[6\]](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?LocID=%22COG%2FLCR20162%2FNAT%2FATO%2Ffp6%22&PiT=99991231235958#fp6)•No dividend arises as a result of the transfer of CGT assets (that are not depreciating assets[\[6A\]](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?LocID=%22COG%2FLCR20162%2FNAT%2FATO%2Ffp6A%22&PiT=99991231235958#fp6A)) by Vitamin Pty Ltd (including any 'deemed dividend' under Division 7A of Part III of the ITAA 1936 or any other provision of the tax law). 12\. Vitamin Pty Ltd recognises any tax liability that may arise under another Commonwealth taxing statute (for example, fringe benefit tax or goods and services tax) or any liability for stamp duty under State legislation. _Setting the tax values of the transferred assets in the hands of the transferee_ 13\. The income tax law applies as if the transfer takes place for the asset's roll-over cost.[\[7\]](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?LocID=%22COG%2FLCR20162%2FNAT%2FATO%2Ffp7%22&PiT=99991231235958#fp7) 14\. The small consulting room is a CGT asset that is not a depreciating asset, revenue asset, or trading stock of Vitamin Pty Ltd. •The trustee is taken to have acquired the consulting room at the time of the transfer for $200,000, being Vitamin Pty Ltd's cost base for the asset immediately before the transfer takes effect.[\[8\]](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?LocID=%22COG%2FLCR20162%2FNAT%2FATO%2Ffp8%22&PiT=99991231235958#fp8) 15\. The goodwill is a CGT asset that is not a depreciating asset, revenue asset or trading stock of Vitamin Pty Ltd. •The trustee is taken to have acquired the goodwill at the time of the transfer for $0, being Vitamin's Pty Ltd's cost base for the goodwill immediately before the transfer takes effect.[\[9\]](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?LocID=%22COG%2FLCR20162%2FNAT%2FATO%2Ffp9%22&PiT=99991231235958#fp9) 16\. The pill press is a CGT asset that is a depreciating asset. •The roll-over cost for a depreciating asset is the transferor's adjustable value just before the transfer takes effect.[\[10\]](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?LocID=%22COG%2FLCR20162%2FNAT%2FATO%2Ffp10%22&PiT=99991231235958#fp10) The adjustable value is $14,000.•The trustee's cost for the pill press is its adjustable value to Vitamin Pty Ltd just before the transfer ($14,000).•The trustee can deduct the decline in value of the pill press using the same method and effective life (or remaining effective life, if using the prime cost method) as Vitamin Pty Ltd was using.[\[11\]](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?LocID=%22COG%2FLCR20162%2FNAT%2FATO%2Ffp11%22&PiT=99991231235958#fp11) 17\. The homeopathic pills are trading stock. •The pills are trading stock on hand in the hands of the trustee.•The roll-over cost for these pills is the cost of the item to Vitamin Pty Ltd ($250)[\[12\]](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?LocID=%22COG%2FLCR20162%2FNAT%2FATO%2Ffp12%22&PiT=99991231235958#fp12), and is deductible.[\[13\]](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?LocID=%22COG%2FLCR20162%2FNAT%2FATO%2Ffp13%22&PiT=99991231235958#fp13) _Acquisition times in the hands of the transferee are set_ 18\. The general CGT acquisition rules apply[\[14\]](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?LocID=%22COG%2FLCR20162%2FNAT%2FATO%2Ffp14%22&PiT=99991231235958#fp14), to determine whether any future capital gain made from a transferred asset is discounted under Subdivision 115-A (the general 50% CGT discount). • This means, apart from pre-CGT assets, the transferee acquires the asset at the time of the transfer. That is, the time of acquisition is not altered by Subdivision 328-G.[\[15\]](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?LocID=%22COG%2FLCR20162%2FNAT%2FATO%2Ffp15%22&PiT=99991231235958#fp15) 19\. Following the transfer of assets to the trustee of the P&S trust, a property investor makes an attractive offer to the trustee for the consulting room. 20\. On 30 September 2017, the trustee enters into an agreement for the sale of the consulting room. The trustee disposes of the room and CGT event A1 happens on 30 September 2017. 21\. The trustee is treated as having acquired the CGT asset at the time of the SBRR transfer, on 1 January 2017. 22\. The trustee is not entitled to access the 50% general CGT discount on disposal, as the trustee acquired the asset less than a year before the CGT event causing this gain. 23\. However, for the purpose of determining eligibility for the 15 year CGT exemption for small businesses, the transferee will be taken as having acquired the asset when the transferor acquired it.[\[16\]](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?LocID=%22COG%2FLCR20162%2FNAT%2FATO%2Ffp16%22&PiT=99991231235958#fp16) 23A. If Pep and Sally transferred their shares in Vitamin Pty Ltd to the trustee of the newly established P&S Trust, Pep and Sally would not be able to choose to apply the SBRR for those shares[\[16A\]](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?LocID=%22COG%2FLCR20162%2FNAT%2FATO%2Ffp16A%22&PiT=99991231235958#fp16A) **_Example 2 - Restructure from partnership to company - cost base of shares_** _Facts_ 24\. Leon and Michelle carry on a car and tyre services business in a partnership. 25\. The active assets of the business are a small suburban garage and goodwill. In 1980, Leon and Michelle acquired the real property (garage) for $80,000, a pre-CGT asset. After 19 September 1985, additional capital expenditure of $40,000 has been outlaid in relation to the garage as an improvement (and is a separate CGT asset[\[17\]](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?LocID=%22COG%2FLCR20162%2FNAT%2FATO%2Ffp17%22&PiT=99991231235958#fp17)). 26\. The liabilities of the business are provisions for employee entitlements totalling $20,000. 27\. They decide to incorporate a new company, LM Services Pty Ltd, and subscribe for 100 original shares with a cost base of $1 each. They maintain the same proportionate ownership. 28\. Leon and Michelle transfer all the assets to LM Services Pty Ltd. The company gives the following as consideration for the transfer of the assets: •10,000 newly issued ordinary shares•assumption of the liabilities for employee entitlements, and•$10,000 cash, borrowed from Leon and Michelle, in their capacity as shareholders. 29\. Both the partnership and LM Services Pty Ltd elect for the SBRR to apply. _Tax values of any membership interests issued for the transfer are set_ 30\. Generally, where membership interests are issued as consideration for the transfer, the cost base of each new membership interest is the sum of the tax values[\[17A\]](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?LocID=%22COG%2FLCR20162%2FNAT%2FATO%2Ffp17A%22&PiT=99991231235958#fp17A) of the transferred assets less any liabilities that the transferee assumes, divided by the number of new membership interests.[\[18\]](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?LocID=%22COG%2FLCR20162%2FNAT%2FATO%2Ffp18%22&PiT=99991231235958#fp18) Step 1 - Tax values of assets 31\. The sum of the roll-over costs excludes the roll-over costs of pre-CGT assets.[\[19\]](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?LocID=%22COG%2FLCR20162%2FNAT%2FATO%2Ffp19%22&PiT=99991231235958#fp19) In this case, the sum is $40,000: •the pre-CGT garage is $80,000, but the amount is excluded•the improvements are $40,000, and•the goodwill is $0. Step 2 - Liabilities 32\. The sum of any liabilities assumed is then subtracted from the sum of roll-over costs. In this case, LM Services Pty Ltd assumes[\[20\]](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?LocID=%22COG%2FLCR20162%2FNAT%2FATO%2Ffp20%22&PiT=99991231235958#fp20) liabilities amounting to $20,000 for employee entitlements. 33\. This means, the first element of the membership interests cost base is $20,000 ($40,000 - $20,000). Step 3 - Consideration other than membership interests 34\. Where the membership interests constitute only a part of the total consideration, the calculated sum[\[20A\]](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?LocID=%22COG%2FLCR20162%2FNAT%2FATO%2Ffp20A%22&PiT=99991231235958#fp20A) needs to be reduced accordingly.[\[21\]](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?LocID=%22COG%2FLCR20162%2FNAT%2FATO%2Ffp21%22&PiT=99991231235958#fp21) In this example, it needs to be reduced by $10,000: •$10,000 cash was provided as part of the consideration for the transfer. Step 4 - Cost base for new membership interest 35\. The aggregate cost base of the new membership interests is therefore $10,000. This amount is then divided by the number of newly-issued ordinary shares (10,000) to determine that the cost base of each share is $1. **_Example 3 - Capital loss on shares attributable to transfer of asset_** _Facts_ 36\. Tom carries on a business of selling vacuum cleaners and cleaning products as a sole trader. He runs his business from a shop that he rents from a company, Cohen Pty Ltd. Tom is the sole director and shareholder of Cohen Pty Ltd. 37\. The cost base and reduced cost base of Tom's shares in Cohen Pty Ltd is $250,000. The cost base of the shop to Cohen Pty Ltd is $100,000. 38\. Cohen Pty Ltd also holds a small office which it acquired recently for $150,000. Cohen Pty Ltd rents out the office to an independent third party, Mark, who uses it to carry out his accountancy business. 39\. Using the SBRR, Tom (as director of Cohen Pty Ltd) decides to transfer the shop into a newly established trust for no consideration (who also elects for the SBRR to apply), leaving Cohen Pty Ltd with the office as its only asset. _Uneconomic losses that are attributable to the transfer are disregarded_ 40\. There are no direct income tax consequences for Cohen Pty Ltd from the transfer of the shop. 41\. Tom will not need to adjust the cost base of his shares in Cohen Pty Ltd to reflect the roll-over. However, if Tom later disposes of the shares for a loss, he will have to disregard the loss unless he can show that it was attributable to something other than the roll-over transaction.[\[22\]](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?LocID=%22COG%2FLCR20162%2FNAT%2FATO%2Ffp22%22&PiT=99991231235958#fp22) 42\. For example, if subsequent to the restructure Tom receives an unexpected offer from Mark to acquire the shares in Cohen Pty Ltd for $175,000 (reflecting the market value of the office), then Tom would need to disregard the capital loss that he would otherwise make on the shares. 43\. This is because Tom's capital loss of $75,000 ($175,000 - $250,000) is wholly attributable to the transfer of the shop. **_Example 4 - Transfer of assets that form a small business pool_** _Facts_ 44\. Sue acquired an existing small business which provides dry cleaning, laundry, home pick-up and delivery services. 45\. During the 2016 income year, Sue purchased new assets for the business for $60,000: •a washer, a tumble dryer, and a dry cleaning machine totalling $10,000, and•2 delivery vans for $25,000 each, totalling $50,000. 46\. Sue chooses to use the small business pool.[\[23\]](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?LocID=%22COG%2FLCR20162%2FNAT%2FATO%2Ffp23%22&PiT=99991231235958#fp23) Using the pool, Sue deducted the business' depreciating assets on a diminishing value method and treated the assets in the pool as a single depreciating asset. 47\. For the 2016 income year, Sue claimed a deduction of $17,500 for the pool ($7,500 for the delivery vans[\[24\]](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?LocID=%22COG%2FLCR20162%2FNAT%2FATO%2Ffp24%22&PiT=99991231235958#fp24) and $10,000 for the rest of the depreciating assets[\[25\]](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?LocID=%22COG%2FLCR20162%2FNAT%2FATO%2Ffp25%22&PiT=99991231235958#fp25)). 48\. In early January 2017, Sue sets up a Clean Dry Unit Trust and transfers the business and all of the assets to the trustee. The trustee issued Sue with an additional new unit as consideration for the transfer of the assets. Both Sue and the trustee elect for the SBRR to apply. _No direct income tax consequences from the transfer of asset_ 49\. Under the SBRR, a transfer of an asset has no direct income tax consequences, except as provided for under Subdivision 328-G.[\[25A\]](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?LocID=%22COG%2FLCR20162%2FNAT%2FATO%2Ffp25A%22&PiT=99991231235958#fp25A) 50\. The effect of the transfer is that Sue no longer holds all the assets in the general small business pool and the trustee of the Clean Dry Unit Trust takes over the depreciating asset pool. 51\. If there had been no transfer, Sue could have claimed a deduction of $12,750[\[26\]](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?LocID=%22COG%2FLCR20162%2FNAT%2FATO%2Ffp26%22&PiT=99991231235958#fp26) for the pool for the 2017 income year. The effect of the SBRR and section 328-247 is that, the $12,750 deductible amount is split equally between Sue and the trustee of the Clean Dry Unit Trust. 52\. For the 2018 and later income years, Sue cannot deduct any further amount under this general small business pool.[\[27\]](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?LocID=%22COG%2FLCR20162%2FNAT%2FATO%2Ffp27%22&PiT=99991231235958#fp27) 53\. For the 2018 income year, the opening pool balance for the trustee of Clean Dry Unit Trust will be $29,750. _Tax values of any membership interests issued for the transfer are set_ 54\. The trustee of the unit trust issues one new unit to Sue as consideration for the transfer. 55\. The cost base of these new membership interests is worked out from the sum of the roll-over costs of the transferred assets that are neither depreciating assets nor pre-CGT assets; and the adjustable values of the transferred assets that are depreciating assets; less any liabilities that the transferee assumes, divided by the number of new membership interests. 56\. In this case, the sum of the roll-over costs is the adjustable values of the transferred assets that are depreciating assets. The adjustable values are the costs of the depreciating assets less its decline in value up to that time, which is: $36,125 ($60,000 less $17,500 less half of $12,750). 57\. The cost base of this one new unit is therefore $36,125. **_Example 5 - Direct tax consequence - FX loan_** _Facts_ 58\. Following from Example 4, prior to the restructure, Sue had taken out a foreign currency denominated loan for $30,000 (Australian dollar equivalent) to finance the business. 59\. As part of consideration for the restructure, the trustee of the Clean Dry Unit Trust assumes Sue's foreign currency liability to the bank through a novation. _Other tax consequences are recognised_ 60\. Forex realisation event 4 occurs when Sue ceases to have an obligation, or part of an obligation, to pay foreign currency. In this case, the event happens when the bank discharges Sue from her liability and sets up a new liability with the trustee of the unit trust. 61\. Due to the foreign currency movement, the Australian dollar equivalent of Sue's liability to the bank is $25,000. Sue makes a forex realisation gain of $5,000, and this is recognised for income tax purposes. 62\. This consequence is recognised because section 328-450 applies to transfers of assets[\[28\]](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?LocID=%22COG%2FLCR20162%2FNAT%2FATO%2Ffp28%22&PiT=99991231235958#fp28) only. **_Example 6 - Indirect tax consequence - subsequent debt forgiveness_** _Facts_ 63\. Dean operates a fishing tour business through a company, where he is the sole director and shareholder. The active assets of the business include a fishing boat, which cost the company $300,000. 64\. In January 2017, a discretionary trust is set up, Dean is one of the beneficiaries and a family trust election is made with Dean as the primary individual. The termination value and adjustable value of the boat is $260,000 at this time. 65\. The company transfers the boat to the trust for $260,000 as consideration, payable within 60 days. Both the company and the trustee choose to apply the SBRR. 66\. The trustee does not pay at that time and enters into a written loan agreement that complies with the requirements of section 109N of the ITAA 1936. 67\. In June 2018, the company executes an effective deed to forgive the loan. _Other tax consequences are recognised_ 68\. A transfer of an asset has no direct income tax consequences, except as provided for under Subdivision 328-G. Related rollover relief for depreciating assets is available under section 40-340. 69\. The subsequent application of Division 7A to the loan, which was created in connection with the transfer of the assets, is an indirect consequence of the transfer and is not turned off by section 328-450. The forgiveness of the loan or failure to make minimum yearly repayments may give rise to a deemed dividend under Division 7A. **Commissioner of Taxation** 13 July 2016 © **AUSTRALIAN TAXATION OFFICE FOR THE COMMONWEALTH OF AUSTRALIA** You are free to copy, adapt, modify, transmit and distribute this material as you wish (but not in any way that suggests the ATO or the Commonwealth endorses you or any of your services or products). #### Footnotes [\[1\]](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?LocID=%22COG%2FLCR20162%2FNAT%2FATO%2Fft1%22&PiT=99991231235958#ft1) Unless otherwise indicated, all legislative references in this Ruling are to the ITAA 1997 as amended by the _Tax Law Amendment_ ( _Small Business Restructure Roll_- _over_) _Act 2016_. # Small business restructure roll-over Transfer active capital gains tax assets between eligible restructuring entities without tax liabilities. **Last updated** 7 May 2025 Print or Download ## On this page - [Eligibility](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/income-deductions-and-concessions/income-and-deductions-for-business/concessions-offsets-and-rebates/small-business-restructure-roll-over#ato-Eligibility) - [Eligible assets](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/income-deductions-and-concessions/income-and-deductions-for-business/concessions-offsets-and-rebates/small-business-restructure-roll-over#ato-Eligibleassets) - [Consequences of choosing the roll-over](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/income-deductions-and-concessions/income-and-deductions-for-business/concessions-offsets-and-rebates/small-business-restructure-roll-over#ato-Consequencesofchoosingtherollover) - [Commissioner's remedial power modification](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/income-deductions-and-concessions/income-and-deductions-for-business/concessions-offsets-and-rebates/small-business-restructure-roll-over#ato-Commissionersremedialpowermodification) ## Eligibility The small business restructure roll-over allows small businesses to transfer active assets from one entity to another without incurring an income tax liability. The roll-over applies if each party to the transfer is one of the following in the income year in which the transfer occurs: - a small business entity - an entity that has an affiliate that is a small business entity - an entity that is connected with a small business entity - a partner in a partnership that is a small business entity. You are eligible for the small business restructure roll-over if: - you are an eligible entity with an aggregated turnover of less than $10 million - from 1 July 2016, you transfer [active assets](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/income-deductions-and-concessions/incentives-and-concessions/small-business-cgt-concessions/small-business-cgt-concessions-eligibility-conditions/active-asset-test) that are capital gains tax (CGT) assets, trading stock, revenue assets or depreciating assets from one entity (the transferor) to one or more other entities (transferees) - transfer of assets forms part of a genuine restructure of an ongoing business as opposed to an artificial or inappropriately tax-driven scheme - the transaction must not result in a change to the ultimate economic ownership (individuals who, directly or indirectly, own an asset) of transferred assets. When there is more than one individual with ultimate economic ownership, there is an additional requirement that each individual’s share of ultimate economic ownership be maintained. Determining whether a restructure is genuine depends on all the facts surrounding the restructure. To provide certainty to small business owners, a safe harbour rule is included that provides an alternative way of meeting the requirement that a restructure is genuine. For more about what we consider to be a genuine restructure of an ongoing business and more about the safe harbour rule, see Law Companion Ruling [LCR 2016/3](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?DocID=COG/LCG20163/NAT/ATO/00001&PiT=99991231235958) _Small Business Restructure Roll-over: genuine restructure of an ongoing business and related matter_. ### Example: ultimate economic ownership does not change Penny runs a furniture manufacturing business as a sole trader. Penny sets up the Just Me Unit Trust with herself as sole unit holder and transfers the active assets of the business to the trust. This would not result in a change in ultimate economic ownership of those assets because Penny continues to hold a 100% interest in the transferred assets. End of example ### Example: changed share of ownership Amy, Joanna and Remy run a delivery business as equal partners and want to transfer their interests in the assets of the partnership to a company. Joanna and Remy are a couple. Amy, Joanna and Remy establish a company, where 300 identical shares are issued as: - 100 shares to Amy - 150 shares to Joanna - 50 shares to Remy. This distribution is because Remy has other income and Joanna and Remy, as a couple, want to lower their overall income tax bill. This shows the company restructure is not a genuine restructure but a tax-driven scheme. The same individuals have ultimate economic ownership of the asset but there is a change in the proportionate share of the ultimate economic ownership. Therefore, Amy, Joanna and Remy are not eligible for the small business restructure roll-over. End of example ### Discretionary trusts and ultimate economic ownership Discretionary trusts may meet the requirements for ultimate economic ownership, for example, where there is no practical change in which individuals economically benefit from the assets before and after the transfer. Family trusts may meet an alternative ultimate economic ownership test where both: - the trustee has made a [family trust election](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/trusts/family-trusts) - every individual who had ultimate economic ownership of the transferred asset before the transfer, and every individual who has ultimate economic ownership after the transfer, must be members of the family group relating to the family trust. ## Eligible assets This roll-over applies to active assets that are CGT assets, depreciating assets, trading stock or revenue assets transferred between entities as part of a genuine restructure of an ongoing business. [Active assets](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/income-deductions-and-concessions/incentives-and-concessions/small-business-cgt-concessions/small-business-cgt-concessions-eligibility-conditions/active-asset-test) are assets used, or held ready for use, while running a business. The roll-over is not available for any other business assets, such as loans to shareholders of a company, as they are not active assets of the business run by the creditor. ## Consequences of choosing the roll-over If you choose to apply the small business restructure roll-over, there are a number of tax consequences: - Assets transferred under the roll-over will not result in an income tax liability arising for either party at the time of the transfer. - The transferor is considered to have received an amount for the transferred asset equal to the transferor's cost of the asset for income tax purposes. - The transferee is considered to have acquired the asset at the time of the transfer for an amount that equals the transferor's cost just before transfer. - There may be potential liabilities such as stamp duty or goods and services tax (GST) consequences to consider before restructuring. - Even though a restructure may meet the roll-over requirements, this does not prevent the general anti-avoidance rule from applying to a scheme involving the application of the roll-over. - For more information about how general anti-avoidance rules may apply to an arrangement or scheme, see [Practice Statement Law Administration PS LA 2005/24](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?docid=PSR/PS200524/NAT/ATO/00001) _Application of General Anti-Avoidance Rules_. ### CGT assets The following tax implications apply to transferred CGT assets: - Pre-CGT assets will retain their pre-CGT status after the transfer. - To be eligible to claim the CGT discount for any subsequent sale of the asset, the transferee will need to wait at least 12 months before a CGT event happens to that asset. - For the purposes of determining eligibility for the small business 15-year exemption, the transferee is considered to acquire the asset when the transferor acquired it. ### Trading stock The roll-over cost of an asset that is trading stock is either the: - cost of the item for the transferor at the time of the transfer - value of the item for the transferor at the start of the income year if the transferor held the item as trading stock at that time. ### Depreciating assets The roll-over prevents the transferor from having to make a balancing adjustment when assets are transferred. This allows the transferee to deduct the decline in value of the depreciating asset using the same method and effective life as the transferor was using. ### Revenue assets If the asset is a [revenue asset](https://www.ato.gov.au/about-ato/using-our-website/definitions), the roll-over cost is the amount that would result in the transferor not making a profit or loss on the transfer. The transferee will inherit the same cost attributes as the transferor just before transfer. ### Shares or interests in a company or trust This roll-over does not require that market value consideration, or any consideration, be given in exchange for the transferred assets. Where membership interests are issued as consideration for the transfer, the cost base or reduced cost base of the new membership interests should be worked out the following way: 1. Add the roll-over costs and adjustable values of the roll-over assets together. 2. Subtract the liabilities the transferee assumes for the assets. 3. Divide the number by the new membership interests. An integrity rule is included to ensure that a capital loss on any direct or indirect membership interest in the transferor or transferee that is made after the roll-over will be disregarded. ## Commissioner's remedial power modification From 8 May 2018, a Commissioner's remedial power instrument ensures no direct income tax consequences from the transfer of depreciating assets undertaken as part of a transaction that otherwise qualifies for small business restructure roll-over relief. - For more information and examples on this determination, see: - [Commissioner's remedial power CRP 2017/2](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?docid=ITD/CRP20172/00001) _Taxation Administration (Remedial Power - Small Business Restructure Roll-over) Determination 2017_ - [Law Companion Ruling and (b) the entity is not a \\* corporate tax entity when the distribution is made; and (c) if the entity is the [trustee](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#trustee) of a trust--the trust is not a \\* complying superannuation entity when the distribution is made; the assessable income of the [partnership](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#partnership) or trust for that [income year](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_year) includes the amount of the \\* [franking credit](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#franking_credit) on the distribution. (2) The amount is in addition to any other amount included in that assessable income in relation to the distribution [under](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#under) any other provision of [this Act](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#this_act). Note: The amount will affect the [income tax liability](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_tax_liability) of a [partner](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#part) in the [partnership](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#partnership), or a beneficiary or the [trustee](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#trustee) of the trust: see Divisions 5 and 6 of [Part](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#part)III of the [Income Tax Assessment Act 1936](http://www.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/). (3) [Subsection](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.10.html#subsection)(4) applies if: (a) a \\* [franked distribution](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#franked_distribution) is made, or \\* flows [indirectly](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#indirectly), to a [partnership](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#partnership) or the [trustee](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#trustee) of a trust in an [income year](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_year); and (b) the assessable income of the [partnership](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#partnership) or trust for that year includes an amount (the [franking credit](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#franking_credit) amount ) that is all or a [part](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#part) of the additional amount of assessable income included [under](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#under) [subsection](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.10.html#subsection)(1) in relation to the distribution; and (c) the distribution flows [indirectly](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#indirectly) to an entity that is a [partner](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#part) in the [partnership](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#partnership), or a beneficiary or the [trustee](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#trustee) of the trust; and (d) disregarding Division 6E of [Part](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#part)III of the [Income Tax Assessment Act 1936](http://www.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/), the entity has an amount of assessable income for that year that is attributable to all or a [part](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#part) of the distribution. (4) Despite any provisions in Divisions 5 and 6 of [Part](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#part)III of the [Income Tax Assessment Act 1936](http://www.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/), the entity's assessable income for that year also includes: (a) in the case of an entity that is a [partner](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#part) in a [partnership](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#partnership)--so much of the [franking credit](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#franking_credit) amount as is equal to the entity's \\* [share](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#share) of the \\* [franking credit](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#franking_credit) on the distribution; and (b) in the case of an entity that is a beneficiary of a trust: (i) so much of the [franking credit](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#franking_credit) amount as is equal to the entity's [share](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#share) of the [franking credit](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#franking_credit) on the distribution; and (ii) the amount mentioned in section 207 \- 37\. Example: A [franked distribution](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#franked_distribution) of $70 is made to the [trustee](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#trustee) of a trust in an [income year](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_year). The trust also has $100 of assessable income from other sources. [Under](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#under) [subsection](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.10.html#subsection)(1), the trust's assessable income includes an additional amount of $30 (which is the [franking credit](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#franking_credit) on the distribution). The trust has a [net income](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#net_income) of $200 for that [income year](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_year). There are 2 beneficiaries of the trust, P and Q, who are presently entitled to the trust's income. [Under](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#under) the trust deed, P is entitled to all of the [franked distribution](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#franked_distribution) and Q is entitled to all other income. The distribution flows [indirectly](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#indirectly) to P (as P has a [share](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#share) of the trust's [net income](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#net_income) that is covered by [paragraph](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.13.html#paragraph)97(1)(a) and has a [share](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#share) of the distribution [under](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#under) section 207 \- [55](http://www.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s55.html) equal to 100% of the distribution). Example: A [franked distribution](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#franked_distribution) of $140 is made to a [partnership](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#partnership). An amount equal to the [franking credit](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#franking_credit) on the distribution ($60) is included in the [partnership](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#partnership)'s assessable income [under](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#under) section 207 \- [35](http://www.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s35.html). Because the [partnership](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#partnership) has losses of $300 from other sources, it has a [partnership loss](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#partnership_loss) of $100 for the [income year](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_year). The [partnership](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#partnership) has 2 equal [partners](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#part). One [partner](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#part) is the [trustee](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#trustee) of a trust and the other [partner](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#part) is an [individual](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#individual). The distribution flows [indirectly](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#indirectly) to each [partner](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#part) [under](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#under) [subsection](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.10.html#subsection)(2). Each [partner](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#part) has a [share](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#share) of the [partnership loss](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#partnership_loss) ($50), a [share](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#share) of the distribution [under](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#under) sections 207 \- [55](http://www.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s55.html) ($70) and a [share](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#share) of the [franking credit](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#franking_credit) [under](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#under) section 207 \- 57 ($30). The [individual](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#individual) [partner](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#part) is allowed a [tax offset](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#tax_offset) of $30 [under](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#under) section 207 \- [45](http://www.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s45.html). Because the trust has $100 of income from other sources, it has a [net income](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#net_income) of $50 for that [income year](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_year) ($100 minus the [share](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#share) of the [partnership loss](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#partnership_loss) of $50). The trust has one [individual](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#individual) as a beneficiary, to whom the distribution flows [indirectly](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#indirectly) [under](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#under) [subsection](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.10.html#subsection)(3). The beneficiary's [share](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#share) of the [franked distribution](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#franked_distribution) is therefore $70 [under](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#under) sections 207 \- [55](http://www.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s55.html) and its [share](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#share) of the [franking credit](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#franking_credit) is $30 [under](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#under) section 207 \- 57\. The beneficiary is also allowed a [tax offset](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#tax_offset) of $30 [under](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#under) section 207 \- [45](http://www.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s45.html). * * * **AustLII:** [Copyright Policy](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/austlii/copyright.html) **\|** [Disclaimers](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/austlii/disclaimers.html) **\|** [Privacy Policy](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/austlii/privacy.html) **\|** [Feedback](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/austlii/feedback.html)

SECT 770.130 **When foreign income tax is considered paid--taxes paid by someone else** (1) This Act applies to you as if you had paid an amount of \* foreign [income tax](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_tax) in respect of an amount (a taxed amount ) that is all or [part](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#part) of an amount included in your \\* [ordinary income](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#ordinary_income) or \\* [statutory income](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#statutory_income) if you are covered by [subsection](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s768.510.html#subsection)(2) or (3) for an amount of foreign [income tax](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_tax) paid in respect of the taxed amount. (2) You are covered by this [subsection](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s768.510.html#subsection) for an amount of \* foreign [income tax](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_tax) paid in respect of a taxed amount if that foreign [income tax](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_tax) has been paid in respect of the taxed amount by another entity [under](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#under) an \\* arrangement with you or [under](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#under) the law relating to the foreign [income tax](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_tax). Example: You are a [partner](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#part) in a [partnership](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#partnership) and the [partnership](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#partnership) pays foreign [income tax](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_tax) on the [partnership](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#partnership) income. (3) You are covered by this [subsection](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s768.510.html#subsection) for an amount of \* foreign [income tax](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_tax) paid in respect of the taxed amount to the extent that: (a) the taxed amount is taken, because of section [6B](http://www.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6b.html) of the [Income Tax Assessment Act 1936](http://www.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/)(the 1936 Act ), to be attributable to another amount of income of a [particular](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#part) kind or source; and (b) foreign [income tax](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_tax) has been paid in respect of the other amount of income; and (c) the taxed amount is less than it would have been if that tax had not been paid. Example: Aust Co (an Australian resident) is the sole beneficiary of an Australian resident trust H and is presently entitled to all the income of trust H. Trust H owns [shares](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#share) in For Co (a foreign company). For Co pays a dividend to trust H and the dividend is subject to [withholding tax](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#withholding_tax) in For Co's country of residence. Trust H allocates to Aust Co, the dividend, as well as other Australian source income trust H earned in the year (none of which was [subject to foreign income tax](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#subject_to_foreign_income_tax)). Aust Co is treated as having paid the foreign [income tax](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_tax) paid by For Co [under](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#under) [subsection](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s768.510.html#subsection)770 \- 130(3). The foreign [income tax](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_tax) is treated as paid in respect of the amount included in Aust Co's assessable income that is attributable to the dividend. * * * **AustLII:** [Copyright Policy](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/austlii/copyright.html) **\|** [Disclaimers](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/austlii/disclaimers.html) **\|** [Privacy Policy](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/austlii/privacy.html) **\|** [Feedback](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/austlii/feedback.html)
