    extract (page read): ## [![](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/images/tiny-austlii.gif)](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/) Commonwealth Consolidated Acts \[ [Index](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/)\] \[ [Table](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/index.html#s102ac)\] \[ [Search](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/sinoform.pl)\] \[ [Search this Act](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/sinoform.pl/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/)\] \[ [Notes](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/notes.html)\] \[ [Noteup](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/sinosrch.pl?query=cth+consol_act+itaa1936240+s102ac)\] \[ [Previous](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s102ab.html)\] \[ [Next](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s102ad.html)\] \[ [Download](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/download.cgi/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240)\] \[ [Help](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/help/legis-help.html)\] * * * ### INCOME TAX ASSESSMENT ACT 1936 - SECT 102AC **Persons to whom Division applies** (1) For the purposes of this Division, a [person](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s202a.html#person) is a prescribed [person](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s202a.html#person) in relation to a [year of income](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#year_of_income) if: (a) the [person](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s202a.html#person) is less than 18 years of age on the last day of the [year of income](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#year_of_income); and (b) the [person](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s202a.html#person) is not an excepted [person](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s202a.html#person) in relation to the [year of income](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#year_of_income). (2) Subject to this section, a [person](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s202a.html#person) (in this [subsection](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s121l.html#subsection) referred to as the minor ) is an excepted [person](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s202a.html#person) in relation to a [year of income](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#year_of_income) for the purposes of this Division if, and only if: (b) the minor was engaged in a full \- time occupation on the last day of the [year of income](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#year_of_income); (c) the minor is a [person](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s202a.html#person): (i) in respect of whom a carer allowance under the [Social Security Act 1991](http://www.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/ssa1991186/)was payable in respect of a period that included the last day of the [year of income](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#year_of_income); or (ii) to whom a disability support pension under that Act was payable in respect of a period that included the last day of the [year of income](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#year_of_income); or (d) the [Commissioner](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#commissioner): (i) has received a certificate issued by a legally qualified medical practitioner certifying that the minor is: (A) a disabled [child](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s202a.html#child), or a disabled adult, within the meaning of Part 2.19 of the [Social Security Act 1991](http://www.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/ssa1991186/); or (B) a [person](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s202a.html#person) who has a continuing inability to work within the meaning of Part 2.3 of the [Social Security Act 1991](http://www.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/ssa1991186/)or is permanently blind; and (ii) is satisfied that, on the last day of the [year of income](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#year_of_income), the minor was a [person](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s202a.html#person) of the kind mentioned in sub \- subparagraph (i)(A) or (B); (da) the minor is the [principal beneficiary](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#principal_beneficiary) of a [special disability trust](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#special_disability_trust); (e) a double orphan pension was payable in respect of the minor under the [Social Security Act 1991](http://www.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/ssa1991186/)in respect of a period that included the last day of the [year of income](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#year_of_income); (f) but for section [1003](http://www.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/ssa1991186/s1003.html) of the [Social Security Act 1991](http://www.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/ssa1991186/), a double orphan pension would have been payable in respect of the minor under that Act in respect of a period that included the last day of the [year of income](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#year_of_income); or (g) the [Commissioner](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#commissioner): (i) has received a certificate issued by a legally qualified medical practitioner certifying that the minor is a [person](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s202a.html#person) who, by reason of a permanent disability, is unlikely to be able to engage in a full \- time occupation; and (ii) is satisfied that, on the last day of the [year of income](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#year_of_income), the minor was such a [person](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s202a.html#person). (3) Where: (a) a double orphan pension was payable, or would, but for section [1003](http://www.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/ssa1991186/s1003.html) of the [Social Security Act 1991](http://www.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/ssa1991186/), have been payable, in respect of a [person](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s202a.html#person) under that Act in respect of a period during a [year of income](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#year_of_income), being a period that included the last day of the [year of income](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#year_of_income); and (b) during the whole of the period referred to in [paragraph](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s124zm.html#paragraph)(a), the [person](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s202a.html#person) was wholly or substantially dependent for support on a [relative](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#relative) or [relatives](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#relative) of the [person](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s202a.html#person); that [person](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s202a.html#person) shall not be taken by virtue of [paragraph](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s124zm.html#paragraph)(2)(e) or (f) to be an excepted [person](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s202a.html#person) in relation to the [year of income](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#year_of_income). (4) Where: (a) the [Commissioner](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#commissioner) is of the opinion that, during a period during a [year of income](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#year_of_income), being a period that included the last day of the [year of income](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#year_of_income), a [person](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s202a.html#person) was a [person](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s202a.html#person) who, by reason of a permanent disability, was unlikely to be able to engage in a full \- time occupation; and (b) during the whole of the period referred to in [paragraph](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s124zm.html#paragraph)(a), the [person](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s202a.html#person) was wholly or substantially dependent for support on a [relative](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#relative) or [relatives](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#relative) of the [person](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s202a.html#person); that [person](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s202a.html#person) shall not be taken, by virtue of [paragraph](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s124zm.html#paragraph)(2)(g), to be an excepted [person](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s202a.html#person) in relation to the [year of income](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#year_of_income). (5) For the purposes of [subsections](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s121l.html#subsection)(3) and (4), a [person](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s202a.html#person) shall be taken to have been wholly or substantially dependent for support on a [relative](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#relative) or [relatives](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#relative) of the [person](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s202a.html#person) during any period during which that [person](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s202a.html#person) resided with a [relative](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#relative) or [relatives](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#relative) of the [person](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s202a.html#person) unless the contrary is established to the satisfaction of the [Commissioner](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#commissioner). (6) Subject to this section, a [person](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s202a.html#person) shall be taken, for the purposes of [subsection](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s121l.html#subsection)(2), to have been engaged in a full \- time occupation on the last day of a [year of income](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#year_of_income) if, and only if: (a) the [person](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s202a.html#person) was, on the last day of the [year of income](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#year_of_income), a [person](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s202a.html#person) engaged in a full \- time occupation; or (b) in a case to which [paragraph](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s124zm.html#paragraph)(a) does not apply--the [person](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s202a.html#person) was engaged in a full \- time occupation during the [year of income](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#year_of_income) for a period of not less than 3 months or for periods the aggregate of which is not less than 3 months. (7) Where: (a) during a period during a [year of income](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#year_of_income), a [person](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s202a.html#person) was engaged in a full \- time occupation; and (b) during the [year of income](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#year_of_income) and after the expiration of that period, the [person](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s202a.html#person) was engaged in a course of full \- time education at a school, college, university or similar institution; no regard shall be had to that period in determining whether the [person](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s202a.html#person) is to be taken, by virtue of [paragraph](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s124zm.html#paragraph)(6)(b), to have been engaged in a full \- time occupation on the last day of the [year of income](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#year_of_income). (8) A [person](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s202a.html#person) shall not be taken to have been engaged in a full - time occupation on the last day of a [year of income](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#year_of_income) unless the [Commissioner](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#commissioner) is satisfied that, on that day: (a) the [person](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s202a.html#person) had the intention of engaging in a full \- time occupation or full \- time occupations during the whole or a substantial part of the next succeeding [year of income](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#year_of_income); and (b) the [person](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s202a.html#person) did not have the intention of engaging in a course of full \- time education at a school, college, university or similar institution at any time during the next succeeding [year of income](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#year_of_income). * * * **AustLII:** [Copyright Policy](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/austlii/copyright.html) **\|** [Disclaimers](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/austlii/disclaimers.html) **\|** [Privacy Policy](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/austlii/privacy.html) **\|** [Feedback](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/austlii/feedback.html)

[[7]] MEDICARE LEVY ACT 1986 - SECT 7 Levy in cases of small incomes — https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/mla1986131/s7.html
    extract (page read): ## [![](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/images/tiny-austlii.gif)](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/) Commonwealth Consolidated Acts \[ [Index](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/)\] \[ [Table](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/mla1986131/index.html#s7)\] \[ [Search](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/sinoform.pl)\] \[ [Search this Act](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/sinoform.pl/au/legis/cth/consol_act/mla1986131/)\] \[ [Notes](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/mla1986131/notes.html)\] \[ [Noteup](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/sinosrch.pl?query=cth+consol_act+mla1986131+s7)\] \[ [Previous](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/mla1986131/s6.html)\] \[ [Next](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/mla1986131/s8.html)\] \[ [Download](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/download.cgi/au/legis/cth/consol_act/mla1986131)\] \[ [Help](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/help/legis-help.html)\] * * * ### MEDICARE LEVY ACT 1986 - SECT 7 **Levy in cases of small incomes** (1) Where the taxable income of a person does not exceed the threshold amount, no levy is payable by the person upon that taxable income. (2) Where the taxable income of a person exceeds the threshold amount but does not exceed the phase \- in limit, the amount of levy payable by the person upon that taxable income but for sections [8](http://www.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/mla1986131/s8.html) and [9](http://www.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/mla1986131/s9.html) shall not exceed 10% of the amount of the excess. (3) Where the net income of a trust estate or a part of that net income, being income in respect of which a person in the capacity of a trustee of a trust estate is liable to be assessed pursuant to section 99 of the Assessment Act, does not exceed $416, no levy is payable by the person upon that net income or part, as the case may be. (4) Where the net income of a trust estate or a part of that net income, being income in respect of which a person in the capacity of a trustee of a trust estate is liable to be assessed and pay tax pursuant to section 99 of the Assessment Act, exceeds $416 but does not exceed $520, the amount of levy payable by the person upon that net income shall not exceed 10% of the amount of the excess. * * * **AustLII:** [Copyright Policy](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/austlii/copyright.html) **\|** [Disclaimers](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/austlii/disclaimers.html) **\|** [Privacy Policy](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/austlii/privacy.html) **\|** [Feedback](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/austlii/feedback.html)

[[9]] INCOME TAX ASSESSMENT ACT 1936 - SECT 102AG Trust income to which Division applies — https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s102ag.html

SECT 102AG **Trust income to which Division applies** (1) Where a beneficiary of a trust estate is a prescribed [person](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s202a.html#person) in relation to a [year of income](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#year_of_income), this Division applies to so much of the [share](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#share) of the beneficiary of the [net income](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s102m.html#net_income) of the trust estate of the [year of income](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#year_of_income) as, in the opinion of the [Commissioner](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#commissioner), is attributable to [assessable income](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#assessable_income) of the trust estate that is not, in relation to that beneficiary, excepted trust [income](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s128a.html#income). (2) Subject to this section, an amount included in the [assessable income](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#assessable_income) of a trust estate is excepted trust [income](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s128a.html#income) in relation to a beneficiary of the trust estate to the extent to which the amount: (a) is [assessable income](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#assessable_income), of a kind covered by [subsection](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s121l.html#subsection)(2AA), of a trust estate that resulted from: (i) a will, codicil or an order of a court that varied or modified the provisions of a will or codicil; or (ii) an intestacy or an order of a court that varied or modified the application, in relation to the estate of a deceased [person](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s202a.html#person), of the provisions of the law relating to the [distribution](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#distribution) of the estates of [persons](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s202a.html#person) who die intestate; (b) is employment [income](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s128a.html#income); (c) is derived by the [trustee](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#trustee) of the trust estate from the investment of any [property](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s121f.html#property) [transferred](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s343.html#transfer) to the [trustee](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#trustee) for the benefit of the beneficiary: (i) by way of, or in satisfaction of a claim for, damages in respect of: (A) loss by the beneficiary of [parental](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#parent) support; or (B) [personal](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s202a.html#person) injury to the beneficiary, any disease suffered by the beneficiary or any impairment of the beneficiary's physical or mental condition; (ii) pursuant to any law relating to worker's compensation; (iii) pursuant to any law relating to the payment of compensation in respect of criminal injuries; (iv) directly as the result of the death of a [person](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s202a.html#person) and under the terms of a policy of life insurance; (v) directly as the result of the death of a [person](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s202a.html#person) and out of a [provident](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s21a.html#provide), benefit, superannuation or retirement fund; (vi) directly as the result of the death of a [person](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s202a.html#person) by an employer of the deceased [person](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s202a.html#person); (vii) out of a public fund established and maintained exclusively for the relief of [persons](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s202a.html#person) in necessitous circumstances; or (viii) as the result of a family breakdown (see section [102AGA)](http://www.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s102aga.html); (d) is derived by the [trustee](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#trustee) of the trust estate from the investment of any [property](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s121f.html#property): (i) that devolved for the benefit of the beneficiary from the estate of a deceased [person](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s202a.html#person); (ii) that was [transferred](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s343.html#transfer) to the [trustee](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#trustee) for the benefit of the beneficiary by another [person](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s202a.html#person) out of [property](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s121f.html#property) that devolved upon that other [person](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s202a.html#person) from the estate of a deceased [person](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s202a.html#person) and was so [transferred](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s343.html#transfer) within 3 years after the date of the death of the deceased [person](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s202a.html#person); or (iii) being a verifiable prize in a legally authorized and conducted lottery and being a prize of which the beneficiary is the beneficial [owner](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s121c.html#owner); or (e) is derived by the [trustee](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#trustee) of the trust estate from the investment of any [property](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s121f.html#property) that, in the opinion of the [Commissioner](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#commissioner), represents accumulations of: (i) [assessable income](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#assessable_income) derived by the [trustee](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#trustee) during a [year of income](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#year_of_income) in relation to which this Division applies, being [assessable income](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#assessable_income) that, in relation to the beneficiary, is excepted trust [income](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s128a.html#income); (ii) [assessable income](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#assessable_income) derived by the [trustee](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#trustee) during a [year of income](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#year_of_income) in relation to which this Division does not apply, being [assessable income](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#assessable_income) that would, in the opinion of the [Commissioner](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#commissioner), have been excepted trust [income](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s128a.html#income) in relation to the beneficiary if this Division were applicable in relation to the [year of income](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#year_of_income) during which the [assessable income](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#assessable_income) was derived; or (iii) [exempt income](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s95.html#exempt_income) derived by the [trustee](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#trustee) to which subparagraph (i) or (ii) would, in the opinion of the [Commissioner](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#commissioner), apply if that [exempt income](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s95.html#exempt_income) had been [assessable income](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#assessable_income). (2AA) For the purposes of [paragraph](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s124zm.html#paragraph)(2)(a), [assessable income](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#assessable_income) of a trust estate is of a kind covered by this [subsection](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s121l.html#subsection) if: (a) the [assessable income](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#assessable_income) is derived by the [trustee](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#trustee) of the trust estate from [property](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s121f.html#property); and (b) the [property](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s121f.html#property) satisfies any of the following requirements: (i) the [property](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s121f.html#property) was [transferred](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s343.html#transfer) to the [trustee](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#trustee) of the trust estate to benefit the beneficiary from the estate of the deceased [person](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s202a.html#person) concerned, as a result of the will, codicil, intestacy or order of a court mentioned in [paragraph](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s124zm.html#paragraph)(2)(a); (ii) the [property](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s121f.html#property) represents accumulations of [income](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s128a.html#income) or capital from [property](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s121f.html#property) that satisfies the requirement in subparagraph (i); (iii) the [property](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s121f.html#property) represents accumulations of [income](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s128a.html#income) or capital from [property](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s121f.html#property) that satisfies the requirement in subparagraph (ii), or (because of a previous operation of this subparagraph) the requirement in this subparagraph. (2A) [Paragraph](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s124zm.html#paragraph)(2)(c) or subparagraph (2)(d)(ii) does not apply unless the beneficiary of the trust concerned will, under the terms of the trust, acquire the trust [property](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s121f.html#property) (other than as a [trustee](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s6.html#trustee)) when the trust ends. (3) Subject to [subsection](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s121l.html#subsection)(4), if any 2 or more parties to: (a) the derivation of the excepted trust [income](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s128a.html#income) mentioned in [subsection](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s121l.html#subsection)(2); or (b) any act or transaction directly or indirectly connected with the derivation of that excepted trust [income](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s128a.html#income); were not dealing with each other at arm's length in relation to the derivation, or in relation to the act or transaction, the excepted trust [income](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s128a.html#income) is only so much (if any) of that [income](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s128a.html#income) as would have been derived if they had been dealing with each other at arm's length in relation to the derivation, or in relation to the act or transaction. This rule was introduced to discourage adults from diverting income to their children. If you aren't an [excepted person](https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/income-deductions-offsets-and-records/income-you-must-declare/your-income-if-you-are-under-18-years-old#Workoutifyouareanexceptedperson) or receiving [excepted income](https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/income-deductions-offsets-and-records/income-you-must-declare/your-income-if-you-are-under-18-years-old#Exceptedincome), you pay tax on that income as below depending on your residency. You pay the same [individual income tax rates](https://www.ato.gov.au/tax-rates-and-codes/tax-rates-australian-residents) as an adult if you're an excepted person or on excepted income. ## If you are a resident | Income for the year | Tax rates | | --- | --- | | $0 – $416 | Nil | | $417 – $1,307 | Nil plus 66% of the excess over $416 (see [Note](https://www.ato.gov.au/tax-rates-and-codes/tax-rates-if-you-re-under-18-years-old#Ifyouareanonresident)) | | Over $1,307 | 45% of the total amount of the income that is not excepted income | Table 1: Tax rates for residents who are under 18 for 2025–26 | Income for the year | Tax rates | | --- | --- | | $0 – $416 | Nil | | $417 – $1,307 | Nil plus 66%of the excess over $416 (see [Note](https://www.ato.gov.au/tax-rates-and-codes/tax-rates-if-you-re-under-18-years-old#Ifyouareanonresident)) | | Over $1,307 | 45% of the total amount of the income that is not excepted income | Table 2: Tax rates for residents who are under 18 for 2020–21 to 2024–25 **Note**: This rate, or if it is greater, the rate payable on eligible taxable income if it were the top slice of total taxable income and the general rates applied. ## If you are a non-resident | Income for the year | Tax rates | | --- | --- | | $0 – $416 | 30% of the entire amount | | $417 – $713 | $124.80 plus 66% of the excess over $416 (see [Note 1](https://www.ato.gov.au/tax-rates-and-codes/tax-rates-if-you-re-under-18-years-old#Howincomeistaxedifyouareunder18)) | | Over $713 | 45% of the entire amount | Table 3: Tax rates for non-residents who are under 18 for 2025–26 | Income for the year | Tax rates | | --- | --- | | $0 – $416 | 30% of the entire amount | | $417 – $713 | $124.80 plus 66% of the excess over $416 (see [Note 1](https://www.ato.gov.au/tax-rates-and-codes/tax-rates-if-you-re-under-18-years-old#Howincomeistaxedifyouareunder18)) | | Over $713 | 45% of the entire amount | Table 4: Tax rates for non-residents who are under 18 for 2024–25 | Income for the year | Tax rates | | --- | --- | | $0 – $416 | 32.5% of the entire amount | | $417 – $663 | $135.20 plus 66% of the excess over $416(see [Note 1](https://www.ato.gov.au/tax-rates-and-codes/tax-rates-if-you-re-under-18-years-old#Howincomeistaxedifyouareunder18)) | | Over $663 | 45% of the entire amount | Table 5: Tax rates for non-residents who are under 18 for 2020–21 to 2023–24 **Note 1**: This rate, or if it is greater, the rate payable on eligible taxable income if it were the top slice of total taxable income and the general rates applied. ## How income is taxed if you are under 18 | If you... | Then... | | --- | --- | | Are an excepted person | your net income is taxed at the same individual income tax rates as an adult | | Only have excepted income, such as part-time employment income | your excepted net income is taxed at the same individual income tax rates as an adult | | Have some excepted income (such as part-time employment income) and some other income (such as a family trust distribution) | - your excepted net income is taxed at the same individual income tax rates as an adult<br>- your other income (after taking away deductions claimed for that income) will be taxed at higher rates | | Only have other income (such as a family trust distribution) | your other income (after taking away deductions claimed for that income) will be taxed at higher rates | Table 5: How income of a person under 18 years old is taxed To check the individual tax rates of an adult, see: - [Tax rates – Australian resident](https://www.ato.gov.au/tax-rates-and-codes/tax-rates-australian-residents) - [Tax rates – foreign resident](https://www.ato.gov.au/tax-rates-and-codes/tax-rates-foreign-residents) QC72762 Print or Download

(2) Your [income tax](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_tax) is worked out by reference to your [taxable income](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#taxable_income) for the [income year](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_year). The [income year](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_year) is the same as the \* financial year, except in these [cases](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.5.html#cases): (a) for a company, the [income year](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_year) is the previous financial year; (b) if you have an accounting period that is not the same as the financial year, [each](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.15.html#each) such accounting period or, for a company, [each](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.15.html#each) previous accounting period is an [income year](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_year). Note 1: The Commissioner can allow you to adopt an accounting period ending on a day other than 30 June. See section [18](http://www.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s18.html) of the [Income Tax Assessment Act 1936](http://www.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/). Note 2: An accounting period ends, and a new accounting period starts, when a [partnership](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#partnership) becomes, or ceases to be, a [VCLP](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#vclp), an ESVCLP, an AFOF or a [VCMP](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#vcmp). See section [18A](http://www.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/s18a.html) of the [Income Tax Assessment Act 1936](http://www.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1936240/). (3) Work out your [income tax](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_tax) for the \\* financial year as follows: ![Start formula Income tax equals open bracket Taxable income times Rate close bracket minus Tax offsets end formula](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/images/C2004A05138_image.3.png) [Method](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.15.html#method) statement Step 1. Work out your [taxable income](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#taxable_income) for the [income year](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_year). To do this, see section 4 \- 15\. Step 2. Work out your basic [income tax liability](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_tax_liability) on your [taxable income](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#taxable_income) [using](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.15.html#using): (a) the [income tax](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_tax) rate or rates that apply to you for the [income year](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_year); and (b) any [special](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.15.html#special) provisions that apply to working out that [liability](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#liability). See the [Income Tax Rates Act 1986](http://www.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itra1986174/)and section 4 \- [25](http://www.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s25.html). Step 3. Work out your [tax offsets](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#tax_offset) for the [income year](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_year). A [tax offset](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#tax_offset)reduces the amount of [income tax](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_tax) you have to pay. For the list of [tax offsets](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#tax_offset), see section [13](http://www.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s13.html)\- 1\. Step 4. Subtract your \\* [tax offsets](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#tax_offset) from your basic [income tax liability](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_tax_liability). The result is how much [income tax](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_tax) you owe for the \* financial year. Note 1: Division 63 explains what happens if your [tax offsets](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#tax_offset) exceed your basic [income tax liability](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_tax_liability). How the excess is treated depends on the type of [tax offset](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#tax_offset). Note 2: Section 4 \- [11](http://www.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itpa1997402/s11.html) of the [Income Tax (Transitional Provisions) Act 1997](http://www.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itpa1997402/)(which is about the temporary budget repair levy) may increase the amount of [income tax](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_tax) worked out [under](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#under) this section. [Income tax](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_tax) worked out on another basis (4) For some entities, some or all of their [income tax](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_tax) for the \* financial year is worked out by reference to something other than [taxable income](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#taxable_income) for the [income year](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_year). [Help](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/help/legis-help.html)\] * * * ### INCOME TAX ASSESSMENT ACT 1997 - SECT 770.10 **Entitlement to foreign income tax offset** (1) You are entitled to a \\* [tax offset](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#tax_offset) for an [income year](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_year) for \* foreign [income tax](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_tax). An amount of foreign [income tax](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_tax) counts towards the [tax offset](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#tax_offset) for the year if you paid it in respect of an amount that is all or [part](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#part) of an amount included in your assessable income for the year. (3) A payment is not the provision of [consideration](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/antsasta1999402/s195.1.html#consideration)if: (a) the payment is made by a \\* [government related entity](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/antsasta1999402/s195.1.html#government_related_entity) to another [government related entity](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/antsasta1999402/s195.1.html#government_related_entity) for making a [supply](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/antsasta1999402/s195.1.html#supply); and (b) the payment is: (i) covered by an appropriation under an \\* [Australian law](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/antsasta1999402/s195.1.html#australian_law); or (ii) made under the National Health Reform Agreement agreed to by the Council of Australian Governments on 2 August 2011, as amended from time to time; or (iii) made under another agreement entered into to implement the National Health Reform Agreement; and (c) the payment is calculated on the basis that the sum of: (i) the payment (including the [amounts](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/antsasta1999402/s195.1.html#amount) of any other such payments) relating to the [supply](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/antsasta1999402/s195.1.html#supply); and (ii) anything (including any payment for any act or forbearance) that the other [government related entity](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/antsasta1999402/s195.1.html#government_related_entity) receives from another [entity](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/antsasta1999402/s195.1.html#entity) in connection with, or in response to, or for the inducement of, the [supply](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/antsasta1999402/s195.1.html#supply), or for any other related [supply](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/antsasta1999402/s195.1.html#supply); does not exceed the supplier's anticipated or actual costs of making those supplies. (4) A payment is not the provision of [consideration](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/antsasta1999402/s195.1.html#consideration)if the payment is made by a \\* [government related entity](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/antsasta1999402/s195.1.html#government_related_entity) to another [government related entity](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/antsasta1999402/s195.1.html#government_related_entity) and the payment is of a kind specified in regulations made for the purposes of this [subsection](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/antsasta1999402/s182.10.html#subsection). "2026-09-28T02:41:41.952Z", "creditsUsed": 5, "concurrencyLimited": false }, "answer": "For a financial assistance payment to be consideration for a supply[[9]](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?LocID=%22GST%2FGSTR20122%2FNAT%2FATO%2Ffp9%22&PiT=99991231235958#fp9) there must be a sufficient nexus between the financial assistance payment made by the payer and a supply made by the payee. A financial assistance payment is consideration for a supply if the payment is 'in connection with', 'in response to' or 'for the inducement of' a supply.[[10]](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?LocID=%22GST%2FGSTR20122%2FNAT%2FATO%2Ffp10%22&PiT=99991231235958#fp10) The test is an objective one.\n\nFurther, in identifying the character of the connection, the word 'for' ensures that not every connection between supply and consideration meets the requirements for a taxable supply. That is, merely having any form of connection of any character between a supply and payment of consideration is insufficient to constitute a taxable supply[[10A]](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?LocID=%22GST%2FGSTR20122%2FNAT%2FATO%2Ffp10A%22&PiT=99991231235958#fp10A).\n\nReference to all of the surrounding circumstances of the arrangement, in particular any written documentation, determines whether a financial assistance payment is 'in connection with', 'in response to' or 'for the inducement of' a supply. The surrounding circumstances may include the statutory purpose of the payer in providing the financial assistance, the activities which are to be undertaken by the payee and any other terms and conditions attached to the payment. However, none of these factors will be determinative on their own and the arrangement must the considered as a whole. The description the parties may give to the arrangement, whilst relevant, is not determinative.[[11]](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?LocID=%22GST%2FGSTR20122%2FNAT%2FATO%2Ffp11%22&PiT=99991231235958#fp11)\n\nFinancial assistance payment made to obtain a right that is a material benefit.\n\nIn some arrangements the payer obtains a material benefit in return for the financial assistance payment. This may occur where the payer is provided with the right to commercially exploit the results of the payee's work in return for the financial assistance payment. In this circumstance, the payment has a sufficient nexus with the supply of the right because the payment is made in connection with, in response to or for the inducement of the supply of the right.\n\nExample 1 - sufficient nexus - payment for the supply of rights\n\nYearning for Learning, a non-profit organisation established to advance teaching and learning, provides financial assistance payments to enable Australian tertiary institutions to undertake research.\n\n20.\n\nTo receive the financial assistance payment, a successful payee must enter into a written arrangement in which the payee agrees to provide Yearning for Learning with the right to use the results of the research in its own enterprise.\n\n22. Under the arrangement the payee makes a supply of rights to exploit the research findings.[[12]](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?LocID=%22GST%2FGSTR20122%2FNAT%2FATO%2Ffp12%22&PiT=99991231235958#fp12) The financial assistance payment has a sufficient nexus with this supply because the payment was made to secure the rights. Therefore the payment is consideration for that supply.\n\nYearning for Learning is entitled to an input tax credit on their acquisition of the rights.\n\nPayments for providing advice and information\n\n24. Providing advice or information is a supply.[[13]](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?LocID=%22GST%2FGSTR20122%2FNAT%2FATO%2Ffp13%22&PiT=99991231235958#fp13) A financial assistance payment has a sufficient nexus with such a supply where the payment is made for the purpose of obtaining the information.\n\n25. A university undertakes various research projects into mental illness. Previously the University carried out a one month study into the psychological impacts of chronic illness. The government pays the university to acquire the rights to use these research findings in its own review of aspects of the health system.\n\nThe payment has a sufficient nexus with the right to the research findings because the payment is made in connection with, in response to or for the inducement of that supply.\n\n27. The university is liable for GST on the supply of the right to the research findings.\n\nPayment for the entry into an obligation to do or refrain from doing something\n\nWhere a supply is constituted by the payee entering into an obligation with the payer to do or refrain from doing something and the payment is made to secure that obligation, there is a sufficient nexus between the payment and the obligation. This is because the financial assistance payment is made in connection with, in response to, or for the inducement of the entry into the obligation.\n\nExample 3 - sufficient nexus - payment for entry into an obligation\n\nSnake Glass Jugglers is a commercial dance troupe that develops and presents performance art in South Australia. It enters into an arrangement with Gooseville Arts Foundation, a body that is established for the purpose of fostering the arts.\n\nTherefore, there is a sufficient nexus between the entry into the obligation and the financial assistance payment such that the financial assistance payment is consideration for that supply.\n\nWhere, in return for a financial assistance payment, the payee promotes the payer's business through promotional material, programs or uniforms or advertises the business at events and in the media, the payment will have a sufficient nexus with the supply of the promotion and advertising.\n\nDemeter Sports Goods, a sporting goods manufacturer, sponsors organisations that provide sport and recreational activities for the health and wellbeing of the community.\n\n34.\n\nThe financial assistance payment is provided on the understanding that it be used to acquire artwork but the local art gallery is not under an enforceable obligation to use the payment in the way specified.\n\nThe mere acknowledgement of the financial assistance payment is not an act which has the character of advertising, or promoting the company. There is nothing else supplied by the art gallery.\n\nThere will be no GST consequences for either party arising from this arrangement.\n\n71. In applying these criteria, the courts have recognised that the criteria may not be absolute and may involve a matter of degree.\n\n72. The fact that a payment is made voluntarily does not of itself mean that it is a gift. Such a payment can be consideration for a supply.[[19]](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?LocID=%22GST%2FGSTR20122%2FNAT%2FATO%2Ffp19%22&PiT=99991231235958#fp19)\n\n73. A payment that is made as a function of government, and does not have the characteristics of benefaction including detached, disinterested generosity,[[20]](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?LocID=%22GST%2FGSTR20122%2FNAT%2FATO%2Ffp20%22&PiT=99991231235958#fp20) is not a gift.\n\n74. In order for the specific exclusion from the definition of 'consideration' to apply,[[21]](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?LocID=%22GST%2FGSTR20122%2FNAT%2FATO%2Ffp21%22&PiT=99991231235958#fp21) the payment must be a gift to a non-profit body.\n\nA supply is not a taxable supply unless there is consideration for the supply.[[36]](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?LocID=%22GST%2FGSTR20122%2FNAT%2FATO%2Ffp36%22&PiT=99991231235958#fp36)\n\n101. 'Consideration' is defined by sections 9-15 and 9-17.\n\n(a) certain payments made by a government related entity to another government related entity;[[41]](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?LocID=%22GST%2FGSTR20122%2FNAT%2FATO%2Ffp41%22&PiT=99991231235958#fp41) or(b) a gift made to a non-profit body.[[42]](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?LocID=%22GST%2FGSTR20122%2FNAT%2FATO%2Ffp42%22&PiT=99991231235958#fp42)\n\nNo consideration - gifts to non-profit bodies\n\nThe making of a gift to a non-profit body is not the provision of consideration.[[43]](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?LocID=%22GST%2FGSTR20122%2FNAT%2FATO%2Ffp43%22&PiT=99991231235958#fp43)\n\nMeaning of non-profit body\n\n105. 'Non-profit body' is not defined in the GST Act. Therefore it takes its ordinary meaning having regard to the context in which it appears. There are two elements to the definition:\n\n• the entity must be a body; and• the body must have the characteristic of being a 'non-profit body'.\n\nThe term 'body' has a broad meaning. It is defined in the Macquarie Dictionary as including '17. A collective group; or an artificial person: body politic, body corporate.'[[44]](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?LocID=%22GST%2FGSTR20122%2FNAT%2FATO%2Ffp44%22&PiT=99991231235958#fp44)\n\n107.\n\nThe term 'gift' is not defined in the GST Act and so takes on its ordinary meaning in the context in which it appears. In Federal Commissioner of Taxation v. The income tax legislation similarly gives special treatment to gifts to some charitable and non-profit bodies.[[49]](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?LocID=%22GST%2FGSTR20122%2FNAT%2FATO%2Ffp49%22&PiT=99991231235958#fp49)\n\nAs explained in TR 2005/13, the courts have described a gift, as ordinarily understood, as having the following characteristics and features:\n\n• there is a transfer of a beneficial interest in property;[[50]](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?LocID=%22GST%2FGSTR20122%2FNAT%2FATO%2Ffp50%22&PiT=99991231235958#fp50)• the transfer is made voluntarily;[[51]](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?LocID=%22GST%2FGSTR20122%2FNAT%2FATO%2Ffp51%22&PiT=99991231235958#fp51)• the transfer arises by way of benefaction;[[52]](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?LocID=%22GST%2FGSTR20122%2FNAT%2FATO%2Ffp52%22&PiT=99991231235958#fp52) and• no material benefit or advantage is received by the giver (payer) by way of return.[[53]](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?LocID=%22GST%2FGSTR20122%2FNAT%2FATO%2Ffp53%22&PiT=99991231235958#fp53)\n\n112. Applying the criteria may involve a matter of degree. Therefore, in determining whether a financial assistance payment is a gift it is necessary to consider the whole of the circumstances surrounding the payment and this may include the role of parties other than the payer and the payee. It is the substance and reality of the payment that has to be ascertained. It is therefore necessary to take account of those acts, transactions, arrangements and circumstances that provide context and the explanation for the payment.\n\nA payment that is made as a function of government, and does not have the characteristics of benefaction including detached, disinterested generosity,[[54]](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?LocID=%22GST%2FGSTR20122%2FNAT%2FATO%2Ffp54%22&PiT=99991231235958#fp54) is not a gift.\n\n114. A payment that has conditions that relate to the payer's right to determine how the gift is to be used can still be a gift.[[55]](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?LocID=%22GST%2FGSTR20122%2FNAT%2FATO%2Ffp55%22&PiT=99991231235958#fp55) Such conditions reflect the terms on which the donor makes, and the donee accepts, the payment.[[56]](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?LocID=%22GST%2FGSTR20122%2FNAT%2FATO%2Ffp56%22&PiT=99991231235958#fp56) The payment may still be a gift if the rights that arise as part of the making of the payment do not directly or indirectly provide a material benefit to the payer or an associate.\n\nIs there a supply?\n\nThe meaning of 'supply' is very broad - it means any form of supply whatsoever[[57]](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?LocID=%22GST%2FGSTR20122%2FNAT%2FATO%2Ffp57%22&PiT=99991231235958#fp57) and includes:\n\n• a supply of goods or services;• a provision of advice or information;• a grant, transfer or surrender of real property;• a creation, grant, transfer, assignment or surrender of any right; or• an entry into, or release from, an obligation to: do anything, refrain from an act, or tolerate an act or situation.[[58]](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?LocID=%22GST%2FGSTR20122%2FNAT%2FATO%2Ffp58%22&PiT=99991231235958#fp58)\n\nNo supply\n\n116. In the context of financial assistance payments where the payment is made for the purpose of support or aid, there may be circumstances where no supply is made by the payee.\n\n117. The case of Chatham Islands Enterprise Trust v. CIR[[59]](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?LocID=%22GST%2FGSTR20122%2FNAT%2FATO%2Ffp59%22&PiT=99991231235958#fp59) is an example of such a situation. In that case, the Crown established a trust, being the Chatham Islands Enterprise Trust as a result of concerns over the provision of essential services for the inhabitants of the Chatham Islands. The Government formally settled the trust and agreed to transfer certain key assets to it in addition to making two payments of $4 million each. The payments were to develop the local economy's commercial operations and retain its infrastructure. The trust set up a number of trading companies to take over various key assets.\n\nIn determining the GST implications of the arrangement Keith J and Blanchard J said the following:\n\nThe trust is not making a supply of anything to the settlor in exchange for, or induced by, the payments; it is the recipient of an endowment to be held upon the terms of the deed. Nor can it, consistently with well-established principles, be said that the trust is performing services for its beneficiaries in return for a consideration provided by the settlor. They are benefited by its activities. In the broadest sense, therefore, it may be said that because it serves their interests it is performing services for them.\n\nAn expectation is created between the parties and nothing more\n\n119. A further example of where there may be no supply is where an agreement between the parties is not binding and creates expectations alone.\n\n120. However, the payee might still make a supply in the absence of enforceable obligations, if there is something else such as goods, services or some other thing passing from the payee to the payer or a third party.[[62]](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?LocID=%22GST%2FGSTR20122%2FNAT%2FATO%2Ffp62%22&PiT=99991231235958#fp62)\n\nSufficient nexus between the financial assistance payment and a supply\n\nIn other GST rulings the Commissioner discusses the close coupling between supply and consideration in the GST Act.[[63]](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?LocID=%22GST%2FGSTR20122%2FNAT%2FATO%2Ffp63%22&PiT=99991231235958#fp63) In determining whether a payment is consideration[[63A]](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?LocID=%22GST%2FGSTR20122%2FNAT%2FATO%2Ffp63A%22&PiT=99991231235958#fp63A) and whether there is a 'supply for consideration' those rulings take the view that:\n\nFurther, in identifying the character of the connection, the word 'for' ensures that not every connection between supply and consideration meets the requirements for a taxable supply. That is, merely having any form of connection of any character between a supply and payment of consideration is insufficient to constitute a taxable supply.[[64A]](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?LocID=%22GST%2FGSTR20122%2FNAT%2FATO%2Ffp64A%22&PiT=99991231235958#fp64A)\n\n122.\n\nSufficient nexus\n\nFor a financial assistance payment to be consideration for a supply it is not sufficient for there to be a supply and a payment.\n\nA financial assistance payment is consideration for a supply if the payment is 'in connection with' a supply. Consideration can also be 'in response to' or 'for the inducement of' a supply.\n\n125. While caution needs to be exercised in applying decisions on connective terms in other contexts, the term 'in connection with' is of wide import[[65]](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?LocID=%22GST%2FGSTR20122%2FNAT%2FATO%2Ffp65%22&PiT=99991231235958#fp65) and has been held to be broader in scope than 'for'. FC of T[[66]](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?LocID=%22GST%2FGSTR20122%2FNAT%2FATO%2Ffp66%22&PiT=99991231235958#fp66), Kitto J considered the meaning of consideration 'for or in connection with' in the context of former section 84 of the Income Tax Assessment Act 1936, a provision which included consideration for or in connection with goodwill in a lease premium. Kitto J held that 'in connection with' was a broader test than 'for' and commented that consideration will be in connection with property where 'the receipt of the payment has a substantial relation, in a practical business sense, to that property'.[[67]](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?LocID=%22GST%2FGSTR20122%2FNAT%2FATO%2Ffp67%22&PiT=99991231235958#fp67)\n\nFCT,[[68]](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?LocID=%22GST%2FGSTR20122%2FNAT%2FATO%2Ffp68%22&PiT=99991231235958#fp68) ( Vidler) the Administrative Appeals Tribunal stated:\n\nThe GST Act uses expressions such as 'make [a] supply for consideration' (s 9-5(a)) and 'consideration for the supply' (s 75-10(2)), but then, in the Dictionary in s 195-1 and also in the definition in s 9-15(1)(a), embraces within the concept of 'consideration' any payment that is made 'in connection with' a supply. The introduction of that broader concept 'in connection with' cannot have been accidental. It must be assumed that the object of the legislation is to cast the net more widely than would have been the case if, in both s 195-1 and s 9-15(1)(a), the relationship between 'supply' and 'consideration' had been governed by the word 'for' rather than the expression 'in connection with'.[[69]](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?LocID=%22GST%2FGSTR20122%2FNAT%2FATO%2Ffp69%22&PiT=99991231235958#fp69)\n\nThe Tribunal then went on to say:\n\n..... It is not sufficient to establish a relationship or an association of some kind between a payment and some act, activity or event that is not a taxable supply, or perhaps not a supply at all, and argue from that position that the payment is not consideration for a supply. For if, despite that relationship or association, there is nevertheless a 'connection' between a payment and some act, activity or event that is a supply, then the payment will form (at least part of) the consideration for that supply.[[70]](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?LocID=%22GST%2FGSTR20122%2FNAT%2FATO%2Ffp70%22&PiT=99991231235958#fp70)\n\nThe nature of the connection between consideration and supply was considered by the High Court in Federal Commissioner of Taxation v. Reliance Carpet Co Pty Ltd[[73]](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?LocID=%22GST%2FGSTR20122%2FNAT%2FATO%2Ffp73%22&PiT=99991231235958#fp73) where it was noted that consideration, as defined, includes amongst other things any payment 'in connection with' a supply of anything. The Court further gave an indication that the connection need not be direct though it did not expand on what the extent of the connection needs to be.[[74]](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?LocID=%22GST%2FGSTR20122%2FNAT%2FATO%2Ffp74%22&PiT=99991231235958#fp74)\n\nA financial assistance payment may have a sufficient nexus with a supply even though it may also serve to fulfil another aspect, or be connected with other aspects, of the arrangement, such as the objectives of the payer, that are not themselves supplies by the payee. What is required is an examination of the facts and circumstances of the transaction as a whole to determine if there is a sufficient nexus between the payment and a supply." }

[[6]] GST and fundraising | Australian Taxation Office — https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/gst-excise-and-indirect-taxes/gst/in-detail/rules-for-specific-transactions/gst-and-fundraising
    extract (page read): [Skip to main content](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/gst-excise-and-indirect-taxes/gst/in-detail/rules-for-specific-transactions/gst-and-fundraising#content) [Skip To search](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/gst-excise-and-indirect-taxes/gst/in-detail/rules-for-specific-transactions/gst-and-fundraising#search-box) [Skip To Alex Virtual Assistant](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/gst-excise-and-indirect-taxes/gst/in-detail/rules-for-specific-transactions/gst-and-fundraising#alex-virtual-assistant) # GST and fundraising When you fundraise, there are situations when GST applies. **Last updated** 10 June 2020 Print or Download ## On this page - [Sales including GST](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/gst-excise-and-indirect-taxes/gst/in-detail/rules-for-specific-transactions/gst-and-fundraising#ato-SalesincludingGST) - [Sales not including GST](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/gst-excise-and-indirect-taxes/gst/in-detail/rules-for-specific-transactions/gst-and-fundraising#ato-SalesnotincludingGST) - [Claiming income tax deductions and GST credits](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/gst-excise-and-indirect-taxes/gst/in-detail/rules-for-specific-transactions/gst-and-fundraising#ato-ClaimingincometaxdeductionsandGSTcredits) When your business runs fundraising, you may be able to claim an income tax deduction. Goods and services tax (GST) may apply to some transactions. Ensure you keep records of all donations made. This will help you prepare your tax return and report GST in your business activity statement (BAS). ## Sales including GST If you run a fundraising event that includes taxable sales, we require you to report these sales as usual. **Example 1: Running a fundraising event (proportion of sales donated)** Sierra runs a coffee shop and is registered for GST. To raise funds for bushfire recovery, Sierra decides to donate $2 from every $4 coffee sold in a week, to a deductible gift recipient (DGR) charity. At the end of the week her sales software shows that she sold 1,000 coffees. She donates $2,000 of the $4,000 of sales to the DGR entity and keeps the receipt. The business has an allowable deduction of $2,000 for the donation. As the $4,000 of coffee sales are in the course of Sierra operating her business, these are taxable sales (subject to GST). Sierra must report the GST from the $4,000 of sales in her BAS as usual. End of example If you facilitate a fundraising event including the supply of a service, we require you to report these sales as usual. **Example 2: Running a fundraising event (facilitates event)** Jurgen is a yoga instructor planning a fundraiser event after a natural disaster. Jurgen is a sole trader registered for GST. His friend supplies a studio space for them to use free of charge. He promotes the event via social media and to his regular client email list. He asks for a contribution of $30 each to participate in the ‘Yoga and meditation for a cause’ class. Clients and their friends attend the event, paying in cash and via EFTPOS on the day. The total raised is $990. The supply (of yoga instructing services) is within the course of Jurgen’s business so these are taxable sales (subject to GST). The GST collected, at 1/11th of the supply, is $90. Jurgen must report the GST from the sales in his BAS. He includes the $900 in his tax return as ordinary income. As he donates $900 to a deductible gift recipient and receives a receipt, Jurgen has an allowable deduction for that donated amount. End of example ## Sales not including GST If you supply a service that is not taxable to support a fundraising event, you do not need to report GST. **Example 3: Business contributing to a fundraising event outside of business enterprise** Vida runs a dance school and is registered for GST. Vida’s friends are planning a fundraiser yoga event. She agrees to them using one of the studios for the event, without charge. Vida does not advertise the event and does not receive any benefits relating to the event. As the business does not receive any benefit, the supply made by Vida (of the space) is not a taxable sale. There will be no GST to report in the BAS. End of example ## Claiming income tax deductions and GST credits If you donate trading stock it may be tax deductible if: - you are donating the trading stock outside the ordinary course of your business - have not claimed an income tax deduction for the forced disposal or death of livestock. Trading stock is anything produced, manufactured, acquired or purchased for the purpose of manufacture, sale or exchange in your business. Live stock is also a trading stock. If you donate trading stock with GST attached to it for fundraising, you may be able to apply for a GST credit when you submit your BAS. **See also:** - [Running fundraising events](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/not-for-profit-organisations/gifts-and-fundraising/fundraising-events/running-fundraising-events) - [Helping in a disaster](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/not-for-profit-organisations/gifts-and-fundraising/helping-in-a-disaster) - [Donations to help disaster victims](https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/financial-difficulties-and-disasters/natural-disaster-support/recovery-following-natural-disasters/donations-and-fundraising-to-help-people-affected-by-natural-disaster) - [Trading stock](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/not-for-profit-organisations/gifts-and-fundraising/tax-deductible-donations/gift-types-requirements-and-valuation-rules/trading-stock) When you fundraise, there are situations when GST applies. From 1 July 2015, the term 'Australia' is replaced in nearly all instances within the GST, Luxury Car Tax, and Wine Equalisation Tax legislation with the term 'indirect tax zone' by the _Treasury Legislation Amendment (Repeal Day) Act 2015_. The scope of the new term, however, remains the same as the now repealed definition of 'Australia' used in those Acts. This change was made for consistency of terminology across the tax legislation, with no change in policy or legal effect. For readability and other reasons, where the term 'Australia' is used in this document, it is referring to the 'indirect tax zone' as defined in subsection 195-1 of the GST Act. ![](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/sgif/pbr/exclamation.gif) This Ruling contains references to provisions of the _A New Tax System (Goods and Services Tax) Regulations 1999,_ which have been replaced by the _A New Tax System (Goods and Services Tax) Regulations 2019._ This Ruling continues to have effect in relation to the remade Regulations. Paragraph 32 of [TR 2006/10](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?LocID=%22TXR%2FTR200610%2FNAT%2FATO%22&PiT=99991231235958) provides further guidance on the status and binding effect of public rulings where the law has been repealed and rewritten. The Ruling explains the Commissioner's view on how the _A New Tax System (Goods and Services Tax) Act 1999_ ('GST Act') applies to vouchers. 2\. This Ruling: •outlines the meaning of 'voucher', for the purposes of Division 100 of the GST Act;•provides guidelines on the identification and treatment of vouchers to which section 100-5 of the GST Act applies;•explains the differing implications on the supply and redemption of vouchers, depending on whether section 100-5 applies;•explains the GST implications of payments received by a supplier from third parties on redemption of a voucher to which section 100-5 applies; and•explains the GST implications of a commission or similar payment in an arrangement covered by section 100-18. 3\. This Ruling does not deal with:- •the application of the GST Act in relation to postage stamps. Under section 100-25, postage stamps are not vouchers for GST purposes; and•the application of section 100-20 vouchers supplied to non-residents and redeemed by non-residents in Australia. 4\. All legislative references in this Ruling are to the GST Act, unless otherwise stated. ### Date of effect 5\. This Ruling explains the Commissioner's view of the law as it applied from 1 July 2000.
