General rule (2) The individual fringe benefits amount is the sum of the employee's share of the taxable value of each fringe benefit that relates to the year of tax and is provided in respect of the employment other than an excluded fringe benefit. What is an excluded fringe benefit ? (3) An excluded fringe benefit is a fringe benefit: (a) that is: (i) constituted by the provision of meal entertainment (as defined in section [37AD](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/fbtaa1986312/s37ad.html), whether or not the employer has elected that Division 9A of Part III apply to the employer); and (ii) not provided under a salary packaging arrangement; or (b) that is a car parking fringe benefit (see [subsection](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/fbtaa1986312/s37.html#subsection)136(1)); or (c) that is: (i) a benefit whose taxable value is wholly or partly attributable to entertainment facility leasing expenses; and (ii) not provided under a salary packaging arrangement; or (e) whose taxable value is worked out under section [59](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/fbtaa1986312/s59.html) (about remote area residential fuel); or (f) whose taxable value is reduced under section [60](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/fbtaa1986312/s60.html) (about remote area housing); or (g) that is an amortised fringe benefit (see [subsection](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/fbtaa1986312/s37.html#subsection)136(1)); or (h) that is a reducible fringe benefit (see [subsection](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/fbtaa1986312/s37.html#subsection)136(1)); or (i) that is a benefit prescribed by the regulations for the purposes of this [paragraph](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/fbtaa1986312/s37.html#paragraph); or (j) that relates to occasional travel to a major population centre in Australia provided to employees and family members resident in a location that is not in or adjacent to an eligible urban area; or (k) that relates to freight costs for foodstuffs provided to employees resident in a location that is not in or adjacent to an eligible urban area; or (l) that is provided to address a security concern: (i) relating to the personal safety of an employee, or an associate of an employee; and (ii) that arises in respect of the employee's employment. If section [135G](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/fbtaa1986312/s135g.html) applies to the employer (4) If: (a) section [135G](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/fbtaa1986312/s135g.html) applies for working out the employer's liability to pay tax for the year of tax; and (b) one or more fringe benefits are provided in relation to the year of tax in respect of the employee's employment by the employer; the employee's individual fringe benefits amount is the amount determined by the employer in writing. This [subsection](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/fbtaa1986312/s37.html#subsection) has effect despite [subsection](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/fbtaa1986312/s37.html#subsection)(2). Note: Section [135G](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/fbtaa1986312/s135g.html) allows use of the employer's aggregate fringe benefits amount for an earlier year of tax in working out the employer's liability for tax for the current year of tax. Determining individual fringe benefits amounts (5) In making a determination under [subsection](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/fbtaa1986312/s37.html#subsection)(4), the employer must: (a) ensure that the total of the amount or amounts determined by the employer under that [subsection](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/fbtaa1986312/s37.html#subsection) for the year of tax equals the aggregate fringe benefits amount used for working out the employer's liability to pay tax for the year of tax; and (b) if that [subsection](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/fbtaa1986312/s37.html#subsection) applies to 2 or more of the employer's employees for the year of tax--act reasonably, having regard to the fringe benefit or fringe benefits provided in relation to the year of tax in respect of each employee's employment. Security concerns relating to employees or associates (6) A fringe benefit referred to in [paragraph](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/fbtaa1986312/s37.html#paragraph)(3)(l) is an excluded fringe benefit only to the extent that its provision is consistent with a threat assessment in relation to the employee or associate made by a person who is recognised by: (a) a relevant industry body or government body; or (b) the Commissioner; as competent to make threat assessments. #### Navigate - [Next Section](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/fbtaa1986312/s5f.html) - [Previous Section](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/fbtaa1986312/s5d.html) - [Table of Provisions](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/fbtaa1986312/#s5e) - [Notes](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/fbtaa1986312/notes.html) #### Print - Print (pretty) - Print (eco-friendly) #### Download - [RTF format - Part 1 (116 MB)](https://www.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/fbtaa1986312.rtf) - [RTF format - Part 2 (112 MB)](https://www.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/fbtaa1986312_2.rtf) * * * - [Plain text (ASCII) (709 KB)](https://www.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/fbtaa1986312.txt) #### Cited By - [NoteUp references](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/sinosrch.cgi?method=boolean&query=%22fbtaa1986312%20s5e%22) #### Join the discussion - [Tweet this page](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?text=%E2FRINGE%20BENEFITS%20TAX%20ASSESSMENT%20ACT%201986%20-%20SECT%205EEmployee%27s%20individual%20fringe%20benefits%20amount%E2%80%9D&url=http://www.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/fbtaa1986312/s5e.html&via=austlii&hashtags=austlii) - [Follow @AustLII on Twitter](https://twitter.com/intent/user?screen_name=AustLII)

[[4]] Reportable fringe benefits | Australian Taxation Office — https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/hiring-and-paying-your-workers/fringe-benefits-tax/fbt-registration-lodgment-payment-and-reporting/reportable-fringe-benefits
    extract (page read): [Skip to main content](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/hiring-and-paying-your-workers/fringe-benefits-tax/fbt-registration-lodgment-payment-and-reporting/reportable-fringe-benefits#content) [Skip To search](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/hiring-and-paying-your-workers/fringe-benefits-tax/fbt-registration-lodgment-payment-and-reporting/reportable-fringe-benefits#search-box) [Skip To Alex Virtual Assistant](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/hiring-and-paying-your-workers/fringe-benefits-tax/fbt-registration-lodgment-payment-and-reporting/reportable-fringe-benefits#alex-virtual-assistant) # Reportable fringe benefits Work out which fringe benefits to report in employees' income information, and calculate the reportable amount. **Last updated** 12 January 2023 Print or Download ## On this page - [What you need to do](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/hiring-and-paying-your-workers/fringe-benefits-tax/fbt-registration-lodgment-payment-and-reporting/reportable-fringe-benefits#ato-Whatyouneedtodo) - [Step 1: Work out which benefits are reportable](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/hiring-and-paying-your-workers/fringe-benefits-tax/fbt-registration-lodgment-payment-and-reporting/reportable-fringe-benefits#ato-Step1Workoutwhichbenefitsarereportable) - [Step 2: Work out if you need to report](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/hiring-and-paying-your-workers/fringe-benefits-tax/fbt-registration-lodgment-payment-and-reporting/reportable-fringe-benefits#ato-Step2Workoutifyouneedtoreport) - [Step 3: Calculate the reportable fringe benefits amount](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/hiring-and-paying-your-workers/fringe-benefits-tax/fbt-registration-lodgment-payment-and-reporting/reportable-fringe-benefits#ato-Step3Calculatethereportablefringebenefitsamount) - [Step 4: Report the employee's amount](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/hiring-and-paying-your-workers/fringe-benefits-tax/fbt-registration-lodgment-payment-and-reporting/reportable-fringe-benefits#ato-Step4Reporttheemployeesamount) ## What you need to do If the total value of the reportable fringe benefits you provide to an employee during the year is more than $2,000, you must report the benefits through Single Touch Payroll or on the employee's payment summary. ## Step 1: Work out which benefits are reportable Most fringe benefits are reportable. However, there are some exceptions. ### Benefits you don't report Some benefits are not reportable, including: - car parking fringe benefits where you provide the car parking facilities for an employee - if you reimburse an employee's expense for car parking and it is an expense payment fringe benefit, it is reportable - car benefits from private use of [pooled or shared cars](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/hiring-and-paying-your-workers/fringe-benefits-tax/fbt-registration-lodgment-payment-and-reporting/reportable-fringe-benefits/reporting-exclusion-for-pooled-or-shared-cars) - [meal entertainment benefits, related travel and accommodation, and entertainment facility leasing benefits](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/hiring-and-paying-your-workers/fringe-benefits-tax/fbt-registration-lodgment-payment-and-reporting/reportable-fringe-benefits/reporting-exclusion-for-entertainment-related-benefits), where these are not provided under a salary sacrifice arrangement - remote area housing assistance, home ownership schemes, and repurchase schemes - the cost of occasional travel to a major Australian population centre for an employee living in a remote area - emergency or other essential health care your employee receives as an Australian citizen or permanent resident - while working outside Australia - for which they can't claim a Medicare benefit - benefits your employee receives to ensure their security and personal safety because of their job. If a benefit is not reportable, you don't include it when: - calculating the total value of benefits provided to an employee - reporting the employee's fringe benefits through Single Touch Payroll or on their payment summary. For a full list of benefits that are excluded from reporting, see [FBT Guide: 5 Reportable fringe benefits](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?DocID=SAV%2FFBTGEMP%2F00006). ### Exempt not-for-profit organisations If a benefit you provide to an employee is exempt _solely_ because your organisation is exempt from fringe benefits tax (FBT), it is a reportable fringe benefit. You need to calculate and report the notional taxable value of the benefit. This means you calculate the taxable value of the benefit as if your organisation was not exempt from FBT. Although these benefits are reportable, they remain exempt from FBT. ### Electric cars Although the private use of an [eligible electric car](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/hiring-and-paying-your-workers/fringe-benefits-tax/types-of-fringe-benefits/fbt-on-cars-other-vehicles-parking-and-tolls/electric-cars-exemption) is exempt from FBT, the benefit is reportable. You will need to work out the notional taxable value of the benefits associated with the private use of the exempt electric car. ## Step 2: Work out if you need to report Add up the taxable value of the reportable fringe benefits for each employee. You need to report for an employee if the taxable value of their reportable fringe benefits is more than $2,000 in the FBT year (1 April to 31 March). When you add up the reportable benefits provided to an employee, include: - the employee's share of any benefits they share with other employees - the value of any benefits provided to the employee's associates, such as their partner. ## Step 3: Calculate the reportable fringe benefits amount The amount you report for an employee is called their reportable fringe benefits amount (RFBA). The RFBA is 'grossed-up' to reflect the pre-tax income the employee would have had to earn, at the highest marginal tax rate (plus the Medicare levy), to buy the benefits themselves. To calculate the RFBA for an employee: - take the total taxable value of the reportable fringe benefits provided to the employee (the amount you worked out at step 2) - multiply this amount by the lower (type 2) gross-up rate. For the FBT year ending 31 March 2022, this rate is 1.8868. You do not use the higher (type 1) gross-up rate to calculate the RFBA. This is the case even if you use the higher rate to calculate the amount of FBT to pay on the fringe benefit. **Example: Working out the reportable fringe benefits amount (RFBA)** During the FBT year (1 April 2021 to 31 March 2022), EFG Pty Ltd provides Derek with several fringe benefits. The benefits, and their taxable value, are: - car parking $450 - car $3,000 - home internet (expense payment fringe benefit) $500. The total taxable value of the fringe benefits is $3,950. However, the car parking fringe benefit is not reportable. Therefore, the total taxable value of the reportable fringe benefits provided to Derek is $3,500. EFG calculates the RFBA as follows: - $3,500 × 1.8868 = $6,603 EFG Pty Ltd reports an RFBA for Derek of $6,603 through Single Touch Payroll for the year ending 30 June 2022. End of example ## Step 4: Report the employee's amount You report each employee's RFBA: - through [Single Touch Payroll](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/hiring-and-paying-your-workers/single-touch-payroll/in-detail/single-touch-payroll-employer-reporting-guidelines/expansion-of-stp-phase-2?page=3#Voluntary_reporting) or on their payment summary - for the income year that ends straight after the FBT year ends. For example, benefits you provide during the FBT year ending 31 March 2022 would be reported through Single Touch Payroll or payment summaries for the income year ending 30 June 2022. The RFBA is not part of your employee's assessable income. You need to report it because it is included in income tests for some government benefits and obligations. ### Employee leaves between 1 April and 30 June If an employee leaves between 1 April and 30 June, and received reportable fringe benefits with a taxable value of more than $2,000 during that period, you report the RFBA in the next income year. For example, if the benefits were provided between 1 April and 30 June 2022, you would report them through Single Touch Payroll or on the employee's payment summary for the income year ending 30 June 2023. You need to do this even though there are no wages or salary to report for that employee for the income year. For more information about reportable fringe benefits, including how to amend a reported amount and exemptions for certain entities and circumstances, see [FBT guide: 5 Reportable fringe benefits](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?DocID=SAV/FBTGEMP/00006&PiT=99991231235958/?page=7#5_6_Employee_s_share). Work out which fringe benefits to report in employees' income information, and calculate the reportable amount. [**Reporting exclusion for pooled or shared cars**](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/hiring-and-paying-your-workers/fringe-benefits-tax/fbt-registration-lodgment-payment-and-reporting/reportable-fringe-benefits/reporting-exclusion-for-pooled-or-shared-cars) Check if private use of a car by multiple employees is excluded from reportable fringe benefits. [**Reporting exclusion for entertainment-related benefits**](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/hiring-and-paying-your-workers/fringe-benefits-tax/fbt-registration-lodgment-payment-and-reporting/reportable-fringe-benefits/reporting-exclusion-for-entertainment-related-benefits) Check if meal entertainment and associated benefits are excluded from reportable fringe benefits. correctness.justification: Every item's treatment matches the reference (health insurance and golf club reportable at $5,700; Qantas Club exempt under s 58Y; telephone allowance as salary excluded by s 136(1); car parking and non-salary-sacrifice meal entertainment excluded under s 5E(3)), and the candidate reaches the golf-club result via s 26-45, an equally sound route to the reference's Div 32 reasoning. The only departure is the final figure of $10,754 versus the reference's $10,755 — a rounding convention the candidate expressly justifies from the ATO's own worked example ($3,500 × 1.8868 shown as $6,603) while flagging the $10,755 alternative, so a small, defended slip rather than an error.

completeness.justification: All reference points are covered: each of the six benefits classified with its statutory basis, the golf club's client-entertainment use addressed (otherwise-deductible defeated by s 26-45), the $2,000 reporting threshold applied, the Type 2 gross-up at 1.8868 applied regardless of Type 1/Type 2 status, and the computation shown step by step; no case law is engaged in the reference and none is required for this compliance calculation.

faithfulness.justification: Roughly 8 of 9 load-bearing claims are anchored at the claim and verified from captured text: s 58Y(2)(c) for the Qantas Club, s 136(1)(f) for the telephone allowance, s 5E(3)(b) for car parking, s 26-45 for the golf club, s 5E(3)(a) for meal entertainment, s 5E(2) for the individual fringe benefits amount, and the $2,000 threshold/lower gross-up/rounding from the ATO page, with statutory words set out verbatim. The material unanchored gap is the private health insurance treatment (the other item that counts), which carries no citation; minor unanchored extras include s 15-2, s 5B(1B)/s 135P TAA and the STP timing.

helpfulness.justification: Directly answers for the 2023 FBT year with a treatment table quoting the operative statutory phrases, a step-by-step calculation a reviewer can follow, professional caveats (rounding convention, assumptions, employer FBT unaffected, RFBA's role in income tests) and a practical reporting action (STP for the income year ending 30 June 2023); tightly structured with no padding or process narration.

citation_grounding.justification: Citations are anchored at the claim and the key statutory propositions rest on captured primary text — s 58Y(1)(a)/(2)(c), s 136(1)(f), s 5E(2)/(3)(a)/(b) and s 26-45(1)-(2) are all captured verbatim and verify the claims citing them; the ATO page [[4]] verifies the $2,000 threshold, the lower-rate gross-up, the non-assessability point and the rounding example. Deductions: the private health insurance treatment has no anchor, the 1.8868 rate is captured only as the rate 'for the FBT year ending 31 March 2022' (correct for 2023 but the 2023 rate itself is not in view), and the s 5B(1B)/s 135P TAA references are unverified.

judge_output.summary: Comprehensive, claim-anchored answer that matches the reference on every item's treatment and on the $5,700 base, departing only by $1 on the final figure under a transparently explained ATO rounding convention supported by the captured ATO example.

SECT 108.10 Losses from collectables to be offset only against gains from collectables ### INCOME TAX ASSESSMENT ACT 1997 - SECT 108.10 **Losses from collectables to be offset only against gains from collectables** (1) In working out your \\* [net capital gain](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#net_capital_gain) or \\* [net capital loss](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#net_capital_loss) for the [income year](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_year), \\* capital losses from \\* collectables can be used only to reduce \\* capital gains from collectables. Note: You choose the order in [which](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.5.html#which) you reduce your capital gains from collectables by your capital losses from collectables. Example: Your capital gains from collectables total $200 and your capital losses from collectables total $400. You have other capital gains of $500\. You have a [net capital gain](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#net_capital_gain) of $500 and a [net capital loss](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#net_capital_loss) from collectables of $200. The losses from collectables cannot be used to reduce the $500 capital gain. (2) A collectable is: (a) \\* artwork, jewellery, an antique, or a coin or medallion; or (b) a rare folio, manuscript or [book](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.15.html#book); or (c) a postage stamp or first day [cover](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.5.html#cover); that is used or kept mainly for your (or your \\* associate's) [personal](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#person) use or enjoyment. (3) These are also collectables : (a) an interest in any of the things [covered](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.5.html#cover) by [subsection](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s87.40.html#subsection)(2); or (b) a debt that arises from any of those things; or (c) an option or right to \\* acquire any of those things. Note: Collectables acquired for $500 or less are exempt. However, you get an exemption for an interest in one only if the [market value](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#market_value) of all the interests combined is $500 or less: see Subdivision 118 \- A. (4) If some or all of a \\* capital loss from a \\* collectable cannot be applied in an [income year](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_year), the unapplied amount can be applied in the next [income year](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_year) for [which](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.5.html#which) your \\* capital gains from \\* collectables exceed your \\* capital losses (if any) from collectables. Example: You have a capital gain from a collectable for the [income year](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_year) of $200 and a capital loss from another collectable of $600. Your capital loss from one collectable reduces your capital gain from the other to zero. You cannot apply the remaining $400 of the capital loss in this [income year](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_year), but you can apply it in a later [income year](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_year). (5) If you have 2 or more unapplied \\* [net capital losses](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#net_capital_loss) from \* collectables, you [must](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.15.html#must) apply them in the order you made them. #### Navigate - SECT 108.20 Losses from personal use assets must be disregarded ### INCOME TAX ASSESSMENT ACT 1997 - SECT 108.20 **Losses from personal use assets must be disregarded** (1) In working out your \\* [net capital gain](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#net_capital_gain) or \\* [net capital loss](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#net_capital_loss) for the [income year](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_year), any \\* capital loss you [make](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#make) from a \\* [personal use asset](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#personal_use_asset) is disregarded. (2) A [personal use asset](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#personal_use_asset)is: (a) a \\* CGT asset (except a \\* collectable) that is used or kept mainly for your (or your \\* associate's) [personal](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#person) use or enjoyment; or (b) an option or right to \\* acquire a \\* CGT asset of that kind; or (c) a debt arising from a \\* CGT event in [which](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.5.html#which) the \\* CGT asset the subject of the event was one [covered](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.5.html#cover) by [paragraph](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s87.35.html#paragraph)(a); or (d) a debt arising other than: (i) in the course of gaining or producing your assessable income; or (ii) from your carrying on a \\* [business](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.15.html#business). Note 1: There is an exemption for a [personal use asset](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#personal_use_asset) you acquire for $10,000 or less: see section 118 \- 10\. Note 2: A debt arising from a CGT event involving a CGT asset kept mainly for your [personal](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#person) use and enjoyment is a [personal use asset](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#personal_use_asset) to prevent any loss arising from the debt being a normal capital loss. (3) A [personal use asset](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#personal_use_asset)does not include land, a \\* [stratum unit](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#stratum_unit) or a building or structure that is taken to be a separate \\* CGT asset because of Subdivision 108 \- D. #### Navigate - Example: On 10 July 2001, Gayle buys a print for $450 and hangs it in her home. On 30 November 2001 she takes the print to her office and hangs it in the lobby. Gayle self assesses the effective life of the print to be 7 years. Gayle sells the print to Anna for $700 on 2 January 2002. How much can Gayle deduct for the 2001 \- 02 [income year](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_year)? The cost of the print is $450. Gayle chooses to use the [prime cost method](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#prime_cost_method) to calculate its decline in [value](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.15.html#value). The print's decline in [value](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.15.html#value) is: ![Start formula $450 times start fraction 177 over 365 end fraction times start fraction 100% over 7 years end fraction end formula](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/images/C2004A05138_image.115.png) = $31 Gayle can deduct $6 as the taxable use portion of the decline in [value](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.15.html#value) [under](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#under) Division 40: ![Start formula start fraction 34 over 177 end fraction times 31 end formula](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/images/C2004A05138_image.116.png) Due to the balancing adjustment event that occurred on 2 January 2002, $54 is included in Gayle's assessable income for the 2001 \- 02 [income year](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_year) [under](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#under) section 40 \- [285](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s285.html). The amount is reduced for non - taxable use by section 40 \- 290\. A capital gain of $202 is disregarded [under](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#under) this section because the asset is a collectable acquired for less than $500. (2) However, there is a [special](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.15.html#special) rule if the \\* collectable is an interest in one of these \\* CGT assets: (a) \\* artwork, jewellery, an antique, or a coin or medallion; (b) a rare folio, manuscript or [book](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.15.html#book); (c) a postage stamp or first day [cover](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.5.html#cover). A \\* capital gain or \\* capital loss you [make](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#make) from the interest is disregarded only if the \\* [market value](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#market_value) of the asset (when you \\* acquired the interest) is $500 or less. Note: If you last acquired the interest before 16 December 1995, a capital gain or loss is disregarded if you acquired the interest for $500 or less: see section 118 \- 10 of the [Income Tax (Transitional Provisions) Act 1997](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itpa1997402/). (3) A \\* capital gain you [make](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#make) from a \\* [personal use asset](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#personal_use_asset), or [part](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#part) of the asset, is disregarded if the first element of the asset's \* cost base, or the first element of its \\* cost if it is a \\* depreciating asset, is $10,000 or less.     extract (page read): [Skip to main content](https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/investments-and-assets/capital-gains-tax/calculating-your-cgt/using-capital-losses-to-reduce-capital-gains#content) [Skip To search](https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/investments-and-assets/capital-gains-tax/calculating-your-cgt/using-capital-losses-to-reduce-capital-gains#search-box) [Skip To Alex Virtual Assistant](https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/investments-and-assets/capital-gains-tax/calculating-your-cgt/using-capital-losses-to-reduce-capital-gains#alex-virtual-assistant) # Using capital losses to reduce capital gains Find out when you can use capital losses to reduce your capital gains, and how to carry forward a net capital loss. **Last updated** 22 June 2026 Print or Download ## On this page - [When to use capital losses](https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/investments-and-assets/capital-gains-tax/calculating-your-cgt/using-capital-losses-to-reduce-capital-gains#ato-Whentousecapitallosses) - [Carrying forward a net capital loss](https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/investments-and-assets/capital-gains-tax/calculating-your-cgt/using-capital-losses-to-reduce-capital-gains#ato-Carryingforwardanetcapitalloss) - [Non-allowable capital losses](https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/investments-and-assets/capital-gains-tax/calculating-your-cgt/using-capital-losses-to-reduce-capital-gains#ato-Nonallowablecapitallosses) - [Capital losses from collectables](https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/investments-and-assets/capital-gains-tax/calculating-your-cgt/using-capital-losses-to-reduce-capital-gains#ato-Capitallossesfromcollectables) - [Company capital losses](https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/investments-and-assets/capital-gains-tax/calculating-your-cgt/using-capital-losses-to-reduce-capital-gains#ato-Companycapitallosses) - [Trust capital losses](https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/investments-and-assets/capital-gains-tax/calculating-your-cgt/using-capital-losses-to-reduce-capital-gains#ato-Trustcapitallosses) - [Exempt entity losses](https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/investments-and-assets/capital-gains-tax/calculating-your-cgt/using-capital-losses-to-reduce-capital-gains#ato-Exemptentitylosses) ## When to use capital losses You use your current year capital losses to offset your current year capital gains. You can choose which capital gains to subtract your capital losses from. If you have any capital gains that are not eligible for the CGT discount, subtract your capital losses from these gains first. This will result in the lowest payable CGT. If you have capital losses from prior years, also known as net capital losses carried forward, you can use them to offset your current year capital gains. If your prior year capital losses extinguished your current year capital gain, you don't have a current year capital gain. As net capital losses can be carried forward indefinitely, there is an order of using your capital losses to offset capital gains. You apply your net capital losses in the order that you make them. There are capital losses you can't use to offset capital gains, they are listed at [non-allowable capital losses](https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/investments-and-assets/capital-gains-tax/calculating-your-cgt/using-capital-losses-to-reduce-capital-gains#Nonallowablecapitallosses). ## Carrying forward a net capital loss If your allowable capital losses are greater than your capital gains, you have a net capital loss. You can carry it forward to later income years to be deducted from future capital gains. You can’t deduct capital losses or a net capital loss from your other assessable income. There is no time limit on how long you can carry forward a net capital loss. ## Non-allowable capital losses You can't deduct capital losses you make from: - [personal use assets](https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/investments-and-assets/capital-gains-tax/list-of-cgt-assets-and-exemptions#ato-Personaluseassets), for example boats or furniture - assets that are [exempt from CGT](https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/investments-and-assets/capital-gains-tax/list-of-cgt-assets-and-exemptions), for example cars and motorcycles - [collectables below a certain value](https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/investments-and-assets/capital-gains-tax/list-of-cgt-assets-and-exemptions#ato-Collectables) - a lease (whether the result of expiry, forfeiture, surrender or assignment) – except if its main purpose is producing income, for example a commercial rental property or a car - paying [personal services income](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/income-deductions-and-concessions/personal-services-income) to yourself through an entity you have set up _._ ## Capital losses from collectables Capital losses from [collectables](https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/investments-and-assets/capital-gains-tax/list-of-cgt-assets-and-exemptions#ato-Collectables) can only be deducted from capital gains made from collectables. They can't be deducted from gains made from other assets. If you don't have a capital gain from another collectable, you can carry forward the capital loss to deduct it against a gain from a collectable in a future year. A collectable isn't subject to CGT if you acquired it for $500 or less (or acquired an interest in it when it had a market value of $500 or less). This means you ignore a capital gain or loss from the collectable. ## Company capital losses A company can deduct previous net capital losses from capital gains in the current year as long as it is either: - substantially under the same ownership and control - still in the same line of business. ## Trust capital losses Capital losses made by a trust can't be distributed to the trust’s beneficiaries. The trust can carry forward its net capital losses and deduct them from capital gains in future years. ## Exempt entity losses Losses made by an entity that is exempt from income tax are disregarded. For more information and help on how to calculate your CGT, see [Calculating your CGT](https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/investments-and-assets/capital-gains-tax/calculating-your-cgt). You work out your [net capital gain](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#net_capital_gain)in this way: Working out your [net capital gain](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#net_capital_gain) Step 1. Reduce the \\* capital gains you made during the [income year](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_year) by the \\* capital losses (if any) you made during the [income year](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_year) as follows: (a) first, reduce any \\* deferred [non-residential capital gains](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#non-residential_capital_gain); (b) then, reduce any \\* deferred [residential capital gains](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#residential_capital_gain); (c) then, reduce any \\* [non-residential capital gains](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#non-residential_capital_gain); (d) then, reduce any \\* [residential capital gains](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#residential_capital_gain). Note 1: Indexation may apply in relation to working out your capital gains: see Divisions 110 and 114. Note 2: Some provisions of [this Act](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#this_act) (such as Divisions 104 and 118) permit or require you to disregard certain capital gains or losses when working out your [net capital gain](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#net_capital_gain). Subdivision 152 \- B permits you, in some circumstances, to disregard a capital gain made from a CGT event happening to a CGT asset you [held](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#held) for at least 15 years. Note 3: If you have more than one capital gain within a category mentioned in [paragraph](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s87.60.html#paragraph)(a), (b), (c) or (d), you can choose the order in [which](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.5.html#which) you reduce them. Step 2\. Apply any previously unapplied \\* [net capital losses](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#net_capital_loss) from earlier [income years](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_year) to [further](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.5.html#further) reduce the amounts (if any) remaining after the reduction of \\* capital gains [under](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#under) step 1. [Make](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#make) the [further](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.5.html#further) reductions in the same order as mentioned in step 1. Note: Section 102 \- 15 explains how to apply [net capital losses](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#net_capital_loss). Step 3. Apply any quarantined amount referred to in [paragraph](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s87.60.html#paragraph)26 \- 155(1)(b) you have for the [income year](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_year) to reduce the amounts (if any) of any \\* deferred [residential capital gains](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#residential_capital_gain) remaining after the reduction of \\* capital gains [under](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#under) step 2. Note: [Subsection](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s87.70.html#subsection)26 \- 155(1) deals with amounts relating to [using](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.15.html#using) or [holding](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#hold) [residential dwellings](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#residential_dwelling) as residential accommodation. Step 4. Apply any quarantined amount referred to in [paragraph](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s87.60.html#paragraph)26 \- 155(1)(b) you have for the [income year](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_year) remaining after step 3 to reduce the amounts (if any) of any \\* [residential capital gains](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#residential_capital_gain) remaining after the reduction of \\* capital gains [under](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#under) step 2. Step 5. Reduce by the \\* discount percentage [each](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.15.html#each) amount of any \\* discount capital gain remaining after the application of steps 1 to 4. Note: Only some entities can have discount capital gains, and only if they have capital gains from certain CGT assets acquired at least a year before making the gains: see Division 115\. Step 6. If any of your \\* capital gains (whether or not they are \\* discount capital gains) remaining after step 5 qualify for any of the small [business](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.15.html#business) concessions in Subdivisions 152 \- C, 152 \- D and 152 \- E, apply those concessions to [each](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.15.html#each) of those capital gains as [provided](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#provide) for in those Subdivisions. Note 1: The basic conditions for getting these concessions are in Subdivision 152 \- A. Note 2: Subdivision 152 \- C does not apply to CGT events J2, J5 and J6. In addition, Subdivision 152 \- E does not apply to CGT events J5 and J6. Step 7. Add up the amounts of any \\* capital gains remaining after step 6. The sum is your [net capital gain](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#net_capital_gain)for the [income year](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_year). Note: For exceptions and modifications to these rules: see section 102 \- 30\. (2) However, if during the [income year](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_year): (a) you became bankrupt; or (b) you were released from debts [under](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#under) a law relating to bankruptcy; any \\* [net capital loss](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#net_capital_loss) you made for an earlier [income year](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_year) [must](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.15.html#must) be disregarded in working out whether you made a \\* [net capital gain](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#net_capital_gain) for the [income year](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_year) or a later one. (3) [Subsection](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s87.70.html#subsection)(2) applies even though your bankruptcy is annulled if: (a) the annulment happens [under](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#under) section [74](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/ba1966142/s74.html) of the [Bankruptcy Act 1966](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/ba1966142/); and (b) [under](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#under) the composition or [scheme](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#scheme) of arrangement concerned, you were, [will](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.5.html#will) be or may be released from debts from [which](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.5.html#which) you would have been released if instead you had been discharged from the bankruptcy. #### Navigate - correctness.justification: The primary answer is entirely correct and matches the reference: shares loss $10,000, costume gain $1,000 (not a collectable per the s 108-10(2) list), table gain $15,000 as a collectable, stamp loss $10,000 quarantined to collectable gains, leaving a $4,000 ordinary net capital loss carried forward and no collectable loss. However, the alternative scenario (if the table were not an antique) is materially miscomputed — the correct result would be a $6,000 net capital gain ($15,000 + $1,000 − $10,000 share loss) plus a $10,000 collectable loss carried forward, not a '$10,000 net capital loss: a $6,000 ordinary loss plus a $4,000 collectable loss'; the aside also includes a mild process reference ('The version I read on AustLII').

completeness.justification: Every reference point is covered: A1 disposal, the costume's exclusion from the s 108-10(2) collectable list, the table as a collectable notwithstanding personal use, the stamp-loss quarantine and ordering against the table gain, the unrestricted share loss, and the $4,000 carry-forward — all laid out in a workings table. It goes beyond the reference with the $500 collectable threshold (s 118-10(1)), the $10,000 PUA threshold (s 118-10(3)), s 108-10(4), s 102-10(2) and the indefinite carry-forward, plus stated assumptions; no judicial authority is needed for this statutory application.

faithfulness.justification: Well over 75% of load-bearing claims are anchored at the claim and verified from captured text: the collectable list (s 108-10(2) [[1]]), the loss-quarantine rule (s 108-10(1) [[1]]), the PUA definition and loss disregard (s 108-20(1)-(2) [[2]]), the $500/$10,000 thresholds (s 118-10(1),(3) [[3]]), the method statement (s 102-5(1) [[5]]), the net capital loss method and s 102-10(2) [[6]], and carry-forward practice ([[4]]) all check out against the captures. The only unverified item is the low-importance s 104-10/CGT event A1 reference in the Assumptions, which has no captured text.

helpfulness.justification: Headline answer up front, per-asset treatment, a clear workings table, carry-forward consequences (s 102-10(2) no deduction against other income, no time limit, no collectable loss carried forward) and sensible assumptions — correctly pitched. It falls short of 5 because the alternative-scenario aside is arithmetically wrong and could mislead in the very contingency it flags, and there is no concrete closing next step (e.g. confirming antique status or reading ATO collectables guidance).

citation_grounding.justification: Every operative statutory proposition is anchored at the claim to captured primary text: the collectable definition and quarantine rule cite s 108-10 with the full section captured [[1]], the PUA definition and loss disregard cite the captured s 108-20 [[2]], the $500/$10,000 exemptions cite the captured s 118-10(1) and (3) [[3]], the method statement cites the captured s 102-5 [[5]], and the net capital loss rules cite the captured s 102-10 [[6]]; the ATO page [[4]] is appropriately used (and captured) only for administrative points (indefinite carry-forward), with multi-source grounding ([[1]]+[[4]]) on the collectable-loss restriction. No irrelevant or unsupportive citations; the only gap is a trivial uncaptured s 104-10 mention in the assumptions.

SECT 110.36 Indexation ### INCOME TAX ASSESSMENT ACT 1997 - SECT 110.36 **Indexation** Indexation for working out capital gains of Australian resident [individuals](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#individual) or trusts for CGT events happening on or after 1 July 2027 (1A) The cost base of a \\* CGT asset also includes indexation of the elements of the cost base (except the third element) for the purposes of working out the \\* capital gain of an [individual](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#individual) or a trust from a \\* CGT event happening in relation to the CGT asset if: (a) the CGT event happens on or after 1 July 2027; and (b) the requirements of Division 114 are met. Note 1: This [subsection](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s87.40.html#subsection) does not extend to foreign residents or [temporary residents](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#temporary_resident) (see section 114 \- [25](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s25.html)). Note 2: This [subsection](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s87.40.html#subsection) is mainly relevant for a trust to the extent that the trust's beneficiaries are [individuals](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#individual) who are Australian residents (see Subdivision 115 \- C and section 114 \- [25](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s25.html)). Note 3: This [subsection](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s87.40.html#subsection) extends to the capital gain of an [individual](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#individual) that is attributable to a [partnership](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#partnership) of [which](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.5.html#which) the [individual](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#individual) is a [partner](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#part). Note 4: If an asset (including a pre \- CGT asset) was [held](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#held) on 30 June 2027, it may be taken to have been sold just before, and reacquired on, 1 July 2027 (see [subsections](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s87.40.html#subsection)112 \- 155(2), 112 \- 165(2) and 112 - 175(2)). For such an asset, indexation because of this [subsection](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s87.40.html#subsection) [will](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.5.html#will) happen only for the period the asset is [held](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#held) on or after 1 July 2027 (see [subsection](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s87.40.html#subsection)960 \- 275(1B)). Indexation for working out capital gains in other circumstances (1) The cost base of a \\* CGT asset also includes indexation of the elements of the cost base (except the third element) for the purposes of working out the \\* capital gain of an entity from a \\* CGT event happening in relation to the CGT asset if: (a) the most recent \\* acquisition of the CGT asset is at or before 11.45 am (by legal time in the Australian Capital Territory) on 21 September 1999; and (b) for an entity that is an [individual](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#individual) or a trust--the CGT event happens before 1 July 2027, and not because of [subsection](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s87.40.html#subsection)112 \- 155(2) or 112 \- 165(2); and (c) the requirements of Division 114 are met. Note: For [paragraph](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s87.35.html#paragraph)(b), indexation is not applicable for working out a capital gain arising: (a) directly from a CGT event taken to have happened [under](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#under) [subsection](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s87.40.html#subsection)112 \- 155(2); or (b) directly or [indirectly](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#indirectly) from a CGT event taken to have happened [under](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#under) [subsection](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s87.40.html#subsection)112 \- 165(2). Instead, capital gains from such CGT events may be discount capital gains. (2) However, for the purposes of working out the \\* capital gain of an entity mentioned in an item of the table from a \\* CGT event happening after 11.45 am (by legal time in the Australian Capital Territory) on 21 September 1999, the cost base includes indexation because of [subsection](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s87.40.html#subsection)(1) only if the entity mentioned in the item chooses that the cost base includes indexation. | Choice of indexation | | --- | | Item | For the purposes of working out the capital

Note 2: For [each](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.15.html#each) CGT asset whose cost base you need to work out, you may either choose to index the expenditure included in the asset's cost base or not [make](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#make) that choice. If you do not choose to index the expenditure, your [net capital gain](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#net_capital_gain) includes only [part](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#part) of your capital gain on the CGT asset as worked out on the basis of the cost base not including indexation and reduced by your capital losses. Note 3: This [subsection](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s87.40.html#subsection) only applies for an [individual](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#individual) or a trust for a CGT event happening before 1 July 2027 (see [paragraph](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s87.35.html#paragraph)(1)(b)). (3) Also, for the purpose of working out the \\* capital gain of a \\* [life insurance company](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#life_insurance_company) from a \\* CGT event happening after 30 June 2000 in respect of a \\* CGT asset that is a \\* complying superannuation asset, the cost base includes indexation because of [subsection](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s87.40.html#subsection)(1) only if the [life insurance company](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#life_insurance_company) chooses that the cost base includes indexation. SECT 114.10 Requirement for 12 months ownership ### INCOME TAX ASSESSMENT ACT 1997 - SECT 114.10 **Requirement for 12 months ownership** (1) You only index expenditure in the \\* cost base of a \\* CGT asset because of [subsection](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s110.55.html#subsection)110 \- 36(1A) or (1) for a \\* CGT event happening in relation to the asset if you, or the entity whose cost base is being worked out, had \\* acquired the asset at least 12 months before the time of the CGT event. Note: Generally, expenditure is indexed from when it is incurred: see [subsection](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s110.55.html#subsection)960 \- 275(1B) or (2). The exception is when there is an acquisition that did not result from a CGT event. The first element in this case is indexed from when the expenditure was paid: see [subsection](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s110.55.html#subsection)960 \- 275(1C) or (3). (2) There are 6 exceptions: • one for \\* CGT event E8: see [subsection](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s110.55.html#subsection)(3); and • one for roll \- [overs](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#over): see [subsections](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s110.55.html#subsection)(4) and (5); and • one for deceased estates: see [subsection](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s110.55.html#subsection)(6); and • one for a surviving joint tenant: see [subsection](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s110.55.html#subsection)(7); and • one for \\* CGT event J1: see [subsection](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s110.55.html#subsection)(8); and • one for a sale and reacquisition taken to have happened [under](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#under) [subsection](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s110.55.html#subsection)112 \- 155(2), 112 \- 165(2) or 112 \- 175(2): see [subsection](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s110.55.html#subsection)(9). CGT event E8 (3) For \\* CGT event E8, the beneficiary indexes the \\* cost bases of the \\* CGT assets of the trust only if the beneficiary \\* acquired the \\* CGT asset that is the interest in the trust capital at least 12 months before \* disposing of it. It does not matter (for indexation from the beneficiary's point of view) how long the [trustee](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#trustee) owned any of the assets of the trust. Same asset roll \- [overs](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#over) (4) The 12 month rule is satisfied for both the entity that owned a \\* CGT asset before a \\* same \- asset roll \- [over](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#over) and the entity that owned it after the roll \- [over](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#over) if the sum of their periods of [ownership](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#owner) of the asset (and the sum of the periods of [ownership](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#owner) of the asset of other entities involved in an unbroken series of roll \- [overs](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#over)) is at least 12 months. Replacement asset roll \- [overs](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#over) (5) The 12 month rule is satisfied for an entity obtaining a \* replacement \- asset roll \- [over](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#over) for a \\* CGT event happening in relation to a \* CGT asset if the period of the entity's [ownership](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#owner) of the original asset (and of other assets for an unbroken series of replacement \- asset roll - [overs](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#over)) and of the replacement asset are together at least 12 months. Example: Company A transfers a CGT asset to Company B (which is a [member](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#member) of the same wholly \- owned group and a foreign resident) 5 months after acquiring it. There is a roll \- [over](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#over) for the transfer [under](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#under) Subdivision 126 \- B. Company B sells the asset 8 months after the transfer. Company A indexes expenditure in its cost base up to the transfer. That cost base becomes the first element of Company B's cost base. Company B indexes its cost base from the transfer to the sale. Deceased estates (6) If a \\* CGT asset you owned just before dying devolves to your \\* [legal personal representative](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#legal_personal_representative) or \\* [passes](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#passes) to a beneficiary in your estate, the 12 month rule applies to the [legal personal representative](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#legal_personal_representative) or the beneficiary as if that entity had \\* acquired the asset when you acquired it. Surviving joint tenant (7) If [individuals](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#individual) own a \\* CGT asset as joint tenants and one of them dies, the 12 month rule applies to the surviving joint tenant as if the surviving joint tenant had \\* acquired the deceased's interest in the asset when the deceased acquired it. Note: The surviving joint tenant is taken to have acquired the deceased's interest in the asset: see section 128 \- 50\. CGT event J1 (8) If \\* CGT event J1 happens, the company that owns the roll - [over](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#over) asset ignores (for indexation purposes) the acquisition rule in [subsection](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s110.55.html#subsection)104 \- 175(8). Sales and reacquisitions taken to have happened in relation to adjustments to the 50% capital gains discount (9) Disregard [subsections](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s110.55.html#subsection)112 \- 155(2), 112 \- 165(2) and 112 \- 175(2) for the purposes of applying the 12 month rule. #### Navigate - SECT 114.1 Indexing elements of cost base ### INCOME TAX ASSESSMENT ACT 1997 - SECT 114.1 **Indexing elements of cost base** (1) In working out the \\* cost base of a \\* CGT asset [under](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#under) [subsection](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s110.55.html#subsection)110 \- 36(1A), index expenditure incurred in [each](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.15.html#each) element (except the third element). Note 1: The expenditure can include giving property (see section 103 \- 5). Note 2: Subdivision 960 \- M shows you how to index amounts (see [subsections](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s110.55.html#subsection)960 \- 275(1B) and (1C) in [particular](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#part)). Note 3: You have to work out the cost base of a CGT asset if a CGT event happens in relation to it or if there is a cost base modification. Note 4: You cannot index expenditure in the third element (costs of [ownership](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#owner)) (see [subsection](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s110.55.html#subsection)960 \- 275(4)). (2) In working out the \\* cost base of a \\* CGT asset [under](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#under) [subsection](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s110.55.html#subsection)110 \- 36(1), index expenditure incurred in [each](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.15.html#each) element (except the third element) at or before the time mentioned in [paragraph](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s110.55.html#paragraph)110 \- 36(1)(a). Note 1: The expenditure can include giving property (see section 103 \- 5). Note 2: Subdivision 960 \- M shows you how to index amounts. Indexation [under](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#under) [subsection](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s110.55.html#subsection)110 \- 36(1) does not take account of inflation after 30 September 1999 (see [subsections](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s110.55.html#subsection)960 \- 275(2) and (3)). Note 3: You have to work out the cost base of a CGT asset if a CGT event happens in relation to it or if there is a cost base modification. Note 4: You cannot index expenditure in the third element (costs of [ownership](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#owner)) (see [subsection](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s110.55.html#subsection)960 \- 275(4)). Note 5: Indexation [under](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#under) [subsection](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s110.55.html#subsection)110 \- 36(1) is not relevant to expenditure incurred after 11.45 am on 21 September 1999 or any expenditure relating to a CGT asset acquired after that time. #### Navigate - [Follow @AustLII on Twitter](https://twitter.com/intent/user?screen_name=AustLII) [[4]] Indexing the cost base | Australian Taxation Office — https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/investments-and-assets/capital-gains-tax/calculating-your-cgt/indexing-the-cost-base extract (page read): [Skip to main content](https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/investments-and-assets/capital-gains-tax/calculating-your-cgt/indexing-the-cost-base#content) [Skip To search](https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/investments-and-assets/capital-gains-tax/calculating-your-cgt/indexing-the-cost-base#search-box) [Skip To Alex Virtual Assistant](https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/investments-and-assets/capital-gains-tax/calculating-your-cgt/indexing-the-cost-base#alex-virtual-assistant) # Indexing the cost base If you acquired an asset before 21 September 1999, you can index its cost base for inflation to reduce capital gains. **Last updated** 29 June 2026 Print or Download Info Alert Recent capital gains tax changes Recent changes to capital gains tax (CGT) announced in the 2026–27 Federal Budget don’t apply to Tax Time 2026. Resources will be available at a later date. ## On this page - [How indexation works](https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/investments-and-assets/capital-gains-tax/calculating-your-cgt/indexing-the-cost-base#ato-Howindexationworks) - [When to use indexation](https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/investments-and-assets/capital-gains-tax/calculating-your-cgt/indexing-the-cost-base#ato-Whentouseindexation) - [How to apply indexation](https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/investments-and-assets/capital-gains-tax/calculating-your-cgt/indexing-the-cost-base#ato-Howtoapplyindexation) ## How indexation works The indexation method adjusts the amount of an asset's costs by the rate of inflation. The adjustment is based on the consumer price index (CPI). The increased cost amounts will reduce your capital gain on the asset. However, you: - must have incurred the costs by 21 September 1999 - can index for inflation only up to 30 September 1999 - can't index the third element of the cost base (costs of owning the asset). ## When to use indexation If your asset is eligible for indexation, it is probably also eligible for the 50% [CGT discount](https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/investments-and-assets/capital-gains-tax/cgt-discount) for individuals. You can use whichever of these methods gives you the best result (the lowest capital gain), but not both. In most cases the discount will give you the best result. Indexation may give you a better result in some situations, for example if you also have capital losses. The [Guide to capital gains tax](https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/capital-gains-tax-guide-2026/about-capital-gains-tax/how-to-work-out-your-capital-gain-or-capital-loss#Choosingtheindexationordiscountmethod) has information on choosing the indexation or discount method. Companies can't use the CGT discount. They should use indexation for assets acquired before 21 September 1999. If you have had a capital loss on an asset, you can't use indexation. ## How to apply indexation You can use the CGT calculator to work out your capital gain. It will automatically apply the method (indexation or discount) that gives you the best result. [Use the Capital gains tax calculator](https://www.ato.gov.au/calculators-and-tools/capital-gains-tax-record-keeping-tool) If you prefer to index your asset cost base yourself, follow these steps. **Step 1: Identify your eligible capital costs** - The costs must be incurred no later than 21 September 1999. - Costs of owning the asset (the third element of the cost base) can't be indexed. **Step 2: For each eligible cost, identify the CPI rate for the quarter in which the cost was incurred** - Use the [CPI quarter-ending rates](https://www.ato.gov.au/tax-rates-and-codes/consumer-price-index) table to find the applicable rate. - If there is a call on partly paid shares or units you acquired after 15 August 1989, you index the full cost of buying them from the date you made the later payment. **Step 3: Calculate the indexation factor for the cost** - Divide 68.7 (the CPI for 30 September 1999) by the CPI from step 2. - Limit the indexation factor to 3 decimal places. If the fourth decimal figure is 5 or higher, round it up (for example, 1.4125 would become 1.413). **Step 4: Multiply the cost by the indexation factor** **Step 5: Total your indexed eligible costs and any non-indexed capital costs** - This is your indexed cost base for the asset. **Step 6: Subtract the indexed cost base from your capital proceeds for the asset** - This is your capital gain for the asset. - Remember, if you index the cost base you can't apply the CGT discount. ### Example: indexing the cost base Val bought an investment property for $150,000 under a contract dated 24 June 1991. She paid: - a deposit of $15,000 on 24 June 1991 - the balance of $135,000 on settlement on 5 August 1991 - stamp duty of $5,000 on 20 July 1991 - solicitor's fees of $2,000 on 5 August 1991 as part of settlement. Val sold the property on 15 October 2025 (the day contracts were exchanged) for $600,000. She incurred costs of: - $1,500 in solicitor’s fees - $15,000 in agent’s commission. Using the steps above, Val works out her cost base as follows. 1. The costs of buying the property are eligible for indexation. They were incurred prior to 21 September 1999. 2. The CPI rates for the quarters in which Val incurred her eligible costs are: - deposit and balance: CPI for June 1991 quarter = 59.0 - stamp duty and solicitor's fees: CPI for September 1991 quarter = 59.3 Although the balance was paid in the September quarter, it is indexed from the date of contract, which was in the June quarter. 3. The indexation factors are: - for the June 1991 quarter: 68.7 ÷ 59.0 = 1.164 - for the September 1991 quarter: 68.7 ÷ 59.3 = 1.159 4. The indexed costs are: Deposit × indexation factor $15,000 × 1.164 = $17,460 Balance × indexation factor $135,000 × 1.164 = $157,140 Stamp duty × indexation factor $5,000 × 1.159 = $5,795 Solicitors’ fees for purchase of property × indexation factor $2,000 × 1.159 = $2,318 5. Val's total cost base is $199,213, made up of: - indexed costs $17,460 + $157,140 + $5,795 + $2,318 = $182,713 - $1,500 solicitor’s fees for sale of property (not eligible for indexation) - $15,000 agent’s commission for sale of property (not eligible for indexation) 6. Using indexation, Val's capital gain for the asset is: Capital proceeds − cost base (indexed) = capital gain $600,000 − $199,213 = $400,787 Val is eligible to use the CGT discount instead of indexation. Unless she has significant capital losses to apply, she will get a better result by using the CGT discount to calculate CGT. End of example For more information on how to calculate your CGT, see [Calculating your CGT](https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/investments-and-assets/capital-gains-tax/calculating-your-cgt).
